docs.text: GCODES FOR DESKTOP CONVEYOR ¶ Communication and Responses ¶ Use 115200 baud for the serial connection, or a TCP connection to the configured Ethernet IP address and port. Send one command per line, terminated by LF ( \n ). CRLF is also accepted. Command names and parameter letters are case-sensitive. Separate parameters with spaces. Angle brackets in usage descriptions are placeholders; do not send the brackets. M315 , M317 , M318 , and M319 process only the first option on a line. Send separate commands to change several settings. Most setting commands return Ok . Queries return their data without a trailing Ok . M312 returns Ok when the position move finishes, rather than immediately. Wait for the expected response before sending the next command. The firmware does not queue position moves. Serial lines are limited to 128 printable characters . An oversized line is discarded and returns Unknown:UART line too long! . Examples show commands and responses separately. Values in response examples are illustrative unless identified as the firmware version or date. Detect Desktop Conveyor COM Port ¶ Send IsXConveyor to identify the conveyor controller. Usage ¶ IsXConveyor Response ¶ YesXConveyor The same firmware also recognizes IsXEncoder and replies with YesXEncoder . Firmware Information ¶ Usage ¶ FirmwareVersion Date Responses for this firmware ¶ FirmwareVersion:1.1.3 FirmwareDate:27/10/2026 Device Address ¶ Read the stored device address with Address , or set it with Address:<value> . The address is a 16-bit unsigned value ( 0 ? 65535 ) and is saved to nonvolatile memory. It is a device identifier, not the Ethernet IP address or TCP port; commands do not need an address prefix. Set an address ¶ Address:1 Response: Ok . Read the address ¶ Address Example response: Address:1 M310 - Set Motion Mode ¶ Select how the motor pins are used. Usage ¶ M310 <mode> Mode Function 0 Output-pin mode. Use M314 to set the motor pin levels directly. 1 Position mode. Use M312 to move and M313 to set the move speed. 2 Velocity mode. Use M311 to set the speed and direction. 3 Potentiometer mode. The onboard potentiometer sets speed and direction. This is not a button-control mode. Changing to a different mode stops the current motion and resets the motor’s position to zero. Sending the mode that is already active leaves the position unchanged. The selected mode is saved to nonvolatile memory. Example ¶ M310 1 Response: Ok . M311 - Set Speed In Velocity Mode ¶ Set the target speed in mm/s. Positive and negative values select opposite directions; 0 requests a stop. Speed changes and direction reversals use the configured acceleration. Use M310 2 for serial/TCP velocity control. In mode 3 , the firmware also accepts M311 , but the next potentiometer update replaces the requested speed. In other modes, the speed request is ignored even though the command returns Ok . Usage ¶ M311 <speed> Example ¶ M311 200 Response: Ok . This acknowledges the command; it does not mean the target speed has already been reached. M312 - Set Position ¶ Move to an absolute motor position in mm, measured from the origin established at startup or the last change of motion mode. The target is not a relative distance from the current position. The conveyor must be in position mode ( M310 1 ) and have no position move in progress. Set the move speed with M313 before starting. A request made in another mode or during an active position move is ignored without a completion response. Usage ¶ M312 <position> Example ¶ M312 123 Response: Ok when the move finishes. If the target is already the current position, Ok is returned immediately. Sending M310 1 again while already in position mode does not reset the origin. M313 - Set Speed In Position Move ¶ Set the speed, in mm/s, for subsequent M312 moves. The firmware uses the absolute value of the supplied speed; direction comes from the target position. Usage ¶ M313 <speed> Example ¶ M313 300 Response: Ok . This speed setting is not saved to nonvolatile memory. M314 - Set Motor Pins Level ¶ An alternate function of the motor pins, available only in output-pin mode ( M310 0 ). This command is not used for normal conveyor motion. Usage ¶ M314 P<pin> V<level> Parameter Values P<pin> 0 : pulse pin (PUL); 1 : direction pin (DIR); 2 : enable pin (EN). V<level> 0 : LOW; 1 : HIGH. Keep the parameter order P then V . Response: Ok . In other motion modes, the pins are not changed even though Ok is returned. M315 - Config Conveyor Parameters ¶ Read the conveyor configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage ¶ M315 M315 S<pulses_per_mm> M315 R<reverse> M315 E<enable> M315 P M315 A<acceleration> Option Function No option Read mode, motor pulses/mm, and direction reversal. S<value> Set motor pulses/mm to match the motor and transmission. Use a positive calibrated value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. E<value> Store the run-with-encoder flag ( 0 or 1 ). In firmware 1.1.3 this flag is not used by the motion-control loop; it does not enable closed-loop positioning. P Stop an active position move immediately and update the estimated motor position from the pulses sent so far. It does not take a target position. A<value> Set acceleration in mm/s?. The firmware uses the absolute value. S , R , E , and A are saved to nonvolatile memory. Setting commands return Ok . The B parameter from X Conveyor is not implemented here. Example: change settings separately ¶ M315 S31.83 M315 R0 M315 A5000 The numbers above are examples, not factory calibration values. Example response to M315 ¶ M:1 S:31.83 R:0 The query returns only M , S , and R ; it does not report acceleration or the encoder flag. After stopping a position move Use M315 P only during an active position move. Firmware 1.1.3 leaves the move counter set after this stop, so change to another mode and back before issuing a new M312 . Changing mode resets the motor position origin. M316 - Set Encoder Mode ¶ Select the encoder reporting mode. Changing the setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the mode to nonvolatile memory. Usage ¶ M316 <mode> Mode Function 0 Absolute position since the last encoder reset. 1 Relative position change since the previous position report. 2 Use encoder channels A and B as input pins with M319 , instead of decoding encoder pulses. Button mode ( 3 ) is not implemented. Example ¶ M316 1 Response: Ok . M317 - Get Position from Encoder ¶ Read the position once, configure periodic position reports, or reset the encoder position. Use one option per command. Usage ¶ M317 M317 T<period_ms> M317 R Option Function No option Return one position report. T<value> Set the report period in milliseconds. Values from 50 to 65535 enable reporting; values below 50 , including 0 , stop it. R Reset the encoder position to zero. This does not reset the motor position used by M312 . Position values use the absolute or relative mode selected by M316 and have two decimal places. Query ¶ M317 Example response: P0:5.32 Enable periodic reports ¶ M317 T500 The command returns Ok , followed by P0:<position> reports every 500 ms. Send M317 T0 to stop reporting. Reset ¶ M317 R Response: Ok . M318 - Set Encoder Parameters ¶ Read the encoder configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage ¶ M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale> Option Function No option Read encoder mode, scale, pulses/mm, reversal, and report period. S<value> Set the calibrated pulses/mm for the selected scale. Use a positive value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. C<value> Select pulse-counting scale: 1 , 2 , or 4 . Each valid setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Changing C does not automatically adjust S ; set both in separate commands. Calibration is loaded from nonvolatile memory, so this reference does not assume a fixed factory pulses/mm value. Example ¶ M318 C2 M318 S10.24 M318 R1 Each setting returns Ok . The pulses/mm value above is an example calibration for scale 2 . Example response to M318 ¶ M:1 C:2 S:10.24 R:1 T:500 M319 - Read Encoder Pin ¶ Read channels A/B as digital inputs, or report changes to their states. Select input-pin mode with M316 2 first; these functions replace normal encoder pulse decoding. Usage ¶ M319 V<pin> M319 T<pin> M319 S<pin> Option Function V<pin> Read the current input state. T<pin> Enable reports when the input state changes. S<pin> Disable reports when the input state changes. Pin 0 is encoder channel A; pin 1 is channel B. Send one option per command. T and S return Ok ; V returns the pin state without a trailing Ok . Example ¶ M319 V1 Example response: I1 V1 Reports use I0 V<state> or I1 V<state> , where state is 0 or 1 . M389 - Enable Ethernet ¶ Set the Ethernet startup-enable flag. M389 1 also initializes Ethernet immediately with the current configuration. Usage ¶ M389 <enable> 1 : set the enable flag and initialize Ethernet. 0 : clear the enable flag. In firmware 1.1.3, this does not close an already running Ethernet server or client connection. The flag is saved with M396 . That command also initializes Ethernet, even when the flag is 0 ; the disabled startup state takes effect after restarting the controller. Response: Ok . Ethernet initialization also sends status messages to the serial connection. M390 - Set Ethernet Port ¶ Set the TCP server port in the current configuration. Save and apply the setting with M396 . Usage ¶ M390 <port> Example ¶ M390 8844 Response: Ok . The source defines 8844 as the initial port, but startup loads the stored configuration. Use M397 to check the configured port. M391 - Set Ethernet IP Address ¶ Set the configured IPv4 address using four decimal octets. 0 0 0 0 selects DHCP when Ethernet is next initialized. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M391 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Static-IP example ¶ M391 192 168 0 2 DHCP ¶ M391 0 0 0 0 Each command returns Ok . M392 - Set Ethernet DNS Address ¶ Set the configured DNS address using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M392 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example ¶ M392 192 168 0 1 Response: Ok . M393 - Set Ethernet Gateway Address ¶ Set the configured gateway using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M393 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example ¶ M393 192 168 0 1 Response: Ok . M394 - Set Ethernet Subnet Address ¶ Set the configured subnet mask using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M394 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example ¶ M394 255 255 255 0 Response: Ok . M395 - Set Ethernet MAC Address ¶ Set the MAC address using six decimal byte values from 0 to 255 , separated by spaces. Convert a hexadecimal MAC address to decimal before sending it. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M395 <byte1> <byte2> <byte3> <byte4> <byte5> <byte6> Example ¶ M395 18 52 86 120 171 5 This represents 12:34:56:78:AB:05 . Response: Ok . M396 - Save and Init Ethernet Port ¶ Save the current Ethernet settings and enable flag to nonvolatile memory, then initialize the Ethernet server with those settings. Usage ¶ M396 Configure network settings through the serial connection, since applying a new configuration can interrupt the TCP connection. M396 initializes Ethernet regardless of the enable flag; set M389 1 before saving if Ethernet should start automatically after a restart. Response: Ok . Initialization status is also printed on the serial connection. M397 - Get Ethernet Port Parameters ¶ Read the configured values held by the firmware. These may include changes that have not yet been saved or applied. Usage ¶ M397 Example response ¶ E_port:8844 E_ip:192.168.0.2 E_dns:192.168.0.1 E_gateway:192.168.0.1 E_subnet:255.255.255.0 E_mac:18.52.86.120.171.5 The MAC address is reported as decimal bytes separated by dots. There is no trailing Ok . M398 - Get Ethernet Local Port Parameters ¶ Read the network stack’s active IP, DNS, gateway, and subnet . The reported port and MAC fields come from the firmware’s configured values. Use this command after Ethernet initialization to check the assigned IP address, especially when using DHCP. Usage ¶ M398 The response uses the same fields as M397 , without a trailing Ok . With DHCP, the configured IP in M397 can be 0.0.0.0 while M398 shows the assigned IP address. The text command IP returns the same network information. When sent through TCP, IP also echoes a line containing IP before the fields; the serial response has no echo line. docs.text: GCODES FOR X CONVEYOR BOARD ¶ Communication and Responses ¶ Use 115200 baud, 8N1 for the serial connection, or TCP to the configured Ethernet IP address and port. Send one command per line, terminated by LF ( \n ). CRLF is also accepted. Command names and parameter letters are case-sensitive. Separate parameters with spaces. Angle brackets in usage descriptions are placeholders; do not send the brackets. M315 , M317 , M318 , M319 , and M331 process only the first option on a line. Send separate commands for several settings. M332 and M333 accept their pin, function, and value together. Most setting commands return Ok . Queries return data without a trailing Ok . M312 returns Ok when the position move finishes rather than immediately. Wait for the expected response before sending the next command. Position moves are not queued. Automatic position or input reports can arrive between command responses. Serial lines are limited to 128 printable characters . An oversized line is discarded and returns Unknown:UART line too long! . Unrecognized M-codes return Unknown:Gcode! . Examples show commands and responses separately. Response values are illustrative except for the stated firmware/mainboard versions and date. Detect Conveyor COM Port ¶ Send IsXConveyor to identify the controller. Usage ¶ IsXConveyor Response ¶ YesXConveyor The firmware also accepts IsXEncoder and replies with YesXEncoder . Firmware and Mainboard Information ¶ Usage ¶ FirmwareVersion Date MainboardVersion Responses for this firmware ¶ FirmwareVersion:2.1.1 FirmwareDate:27/10/2026 MainboardVersion:2.1 Device Address ¶ Read the stored device identifier with Address , or set it with Address:<value> . The value is an unsigned 16-bit number ( 0 ? 65535 ) saved to nonvolatile memory. It is not an IP address or TCP port, and commands do not require an address prefix. Set an address ¶ Address:1 Response: Ok . Read the address ¶ Address Example response: Address:1 Reset Controller ¶ Restart the controller with the case-sensitive text command Reset . This restarts the firmware; it does not restore factory configuration. Usage ¶ Reset The controller prints XConveyor Reset to the serial connection , even if the command was sent through TCP, then restarts after about 100 ms. There is no Ok response. Reconnect after the controller starts again. I/O Pin Numbering ¶ The four dedicated inputs/outputs use zero-based command indices. They are separate from the encoder channels and motor pins. Command index Dedicated input Dedicated output 0 Input 1 Output 1 1 Input 2 Output 2 2 Input 3 Output 3 3 Input 4 Output 4 Use M330 ? M333 for these dedicated I/O pins. M319 instead uses 0 / 1 for encoder channels A/B; M314 uses 0 / 1 / 2 for motor PUL/DIR/EN. XConveyor ¶ Motor control, dedicated digital I/O, and Ethernet configuration commands. M310 - Set Motion Mode ¶ Select the motor-control mode. Usage ¶ M310 <mode> Mode Function 0 Output-pin mode. Control motor PUL/DIR/EN directly with M314 . 1 Position mode. Use M312 to move and M313 to set the move speed. 2 Velocity mode. Use M311 to set speed and direction. 3 Input-control mode. Functions assigned with M332 can change speed, move a relative distance, or stop. Encoder-button control with M316 3 also requires this mode. Changing to a different mode stops motion and resets the motor position, input-speed target, and position-reached state. Resending the mode already active does not reset the motor position. The mode is saved to nonvolatile memory. Input mode also accepts M311 , subject to its motion-state restrictions. It is not potentiometer mode. Example ¶ M310 3 Response: Ok . M311 - Set Speed In Velocity Mode ¶ Set the signed target speed in mm/s. Positive and negative values select opposite directions; 0 requests a stop. Acceleration is applied to speed changes, and a direction reversal decelerates to zero before reversing. The command acts in velocity mode ( M310 2 ) or input mode ( M310 3 ). It does not interrupt an active position move. Requests in other modes or during a position move are ignored even though Ok is returned. Usage ¶ M311 <speed> Example ¶ M311 200 Response: Ok . This acknowledges the request, not that the target speed has been reached. The requested speed is limited by the motor pulse calibration and the maximum step rate: 20000 / pulses_per_mm in mm/s. This firmware limit is not the conveyor’s mechanical speed rating. M312 - Set Position ¶ Move to an absolute motor position in mm, referenced to startup or the last actual change of motion mode. This is different from the relative-distance input function M332 F3 . Use position mode ( M310 1 ) before sending this command. A new position target is not queued while a position move is already running. Usage ¶ M312 <position> Example ¶ M312 123 Response: Ok when the move finishes. If the target already equals the current position, Ok is returned immediately. A request ignored because of mode or motion state has no completion response. Set the move speed with M313 . Resending M310 1 while already in position mode does not reset the origin. M313 - Set Speed In Position Move ¶ Set the speed in mm/s for subsequent position moves, including relative moves triggered through M332 F3 . The absolute value is used and is limited to the maximum step rate for the configured motor pulses/mm. Usage ¶ M313 <speed> Example ¶ M313 300 Response: Ok . This setting is saved to nonvolatile memory in X Conveyor firmware 2.1.1. If no valid stored position speed is available at startup, the firmware uses 50 mm/s. M314 - Set Motor Pins Level ¶ An alternate function of the motor pins, available only in output-pin mode ( M310 0 ). This command is not used for normal conveyor motion. Usage ¶ M314 P<pin> V<level> Parameter Values P<pin> 0 : pulse pin (PUL); 1 : direction pin (DIR); 2 : enable pin (EN). V<level> 0 : LOW; 1 : HIGH. Keep the parameter order P then V . Response: Ok . In other motion modes, the pins are not changed even though Ok is returned. M315 - Config Conveyor Parameters ¶ Read the conveyor configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage ¶ M315 M315 S<pulses_per_mm> M315 R<reverse> M315 E<enable> M315 P M315 A<acceleration> M315 B<button_start_speed> Option Function No option Read mode, motor pulses/mm, and direction reversal. S<value> Set motor pulses/mm to match the motor and transmission. Use a positive calibrated value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. Configure this while the conveyor is stopped. E<value> Store the run-with-encoder flag ( 0 or 1 ). In firmware 2.1.1 it is not used by the motion-control loop and does not enable closed-loop positioning. P Stop an active position move immediately and update the estimated motor position from pulses already sent. It does not take a target position. A<value> Set acceleration in mm/s?. Use a nonnegative value; 0 requests speed changes without an acceleration ramp. B<value> Set the start speed used when holding encoder button A in M316 3 / M310 3 . This is not the speed step of the dedicated inputs configured with M332 . S , R , E , and A save the configuration to nonvolatile memory. B updates the button-start speed in RAM but does not itself save it. Setting commands return Ok . Example: send settings separately ¶ M315 S31.83 M315 R0 M315 A1000 These numbers are examples, not factory calibration values. Example response to M315 ¶ M:1 S:31.83 R:0 The query returns only M , S , and R ; acceleration, the encoder flag, and button-start speed are not included. Use M315 P during a position move. This firmware clears the move counter after the stop, so a subsequent M312 can start without changing mode or resetting the position origin. M330 - Set Output Pin ¶ Set one of the four dedicated outputs. The output must have function F0 selected with M333 before it can be controlled manually. Usage ¶ M330 P<pin> V<state> Parameter Values P<pin> Output index 0 ? 3 , corresponding to Output 1?4. V<state> 0 : off; 1 : on. Keep the parameter order P then V . Example: manually activate Output 1 ¶ M333 P0 F0 M330 P0 V1 Each command returns Ok . If the output has an automatic function ( F1 or F2 ), M330 returns Unknown:Output has function! and leaves it under automatic control. M331 - Read Input Pin ¶ Read one of the four dedicated inputs, or enable/disable reports when its logic state changes. Send one option per command. Usage ¶ M331 V<pin> M331 T<pin> M331 S<pin> Option Function V<pin> Read the current input state. T<pin> Enable reports when the state changes. S<pin> Disable change reports. Use pin indices 0 ? 3 for Input 1?4. V returns data without Ok ; T and S return Ok . Automatic reporting is separate from the input’s assigned motion function and is not saved across restarts. Example: read Input 1 ¶ M331 V0 Example response: I0 V1 M331 T0 enables further I0 V<state> reports. M331 S0 stops them. These are raw logic-state changes, not the debounced motion triggers used by M332 . M332 - Configure Input Pin ¶ Assign a motion function to a dedicated input. These functions are active only in input-control mode ( M310 3 ) . Pin indices are 0 ? 3 . Usage ¶ M332 M332 I<pin> M332 I<pin> F<function> V<value> No options: return the configuration of all four inputs. I<pin> alone: return that input’s configuration. I<pin> F<function> : set the function. Add V<value> to set the function value. Parameter order is flexible. Function Behavior Value F0 No motion function. Reading/reporting through M331 remains available. Ignored. F1 Increase the input controller’s speed target. Step in mm/s. F2 Decrease the input controller’s speed target. Step in mm/s. F3 Move by a relative distance from the current motor position. Signed distance in mm. F4 Stop an active position move immediately, or request zero velocity for a speed run. Ignored. A function triggers when the input logic becomes 1 after remaining stable for more than 25 ms . Holding F1 / F2 for more than 1.5 seconds repeats the speed step at approximately 100 ms intervals. F1 / F2 are ignored during a position move. F3 is accepted only when the conveyor is stopped with no pending reversal or position move, and uses the speed set by M313 . F4 handles both motion types in input mode. The input-speed target starts at zero when the motion mode changes. Example: assign speed-up to Input 1 and stop to Input 2 ¶ M332 I0 F1 V50 M332 I1 F4 V0 M310 3 Each setting returns Ok . Functions and values are saved to nonvolatile memory. Example response to M332 I0 ¶ I0 F1 V50.00 M332 without options returns one line per input, I0 through I3 , with no trailing Ok . M333 - Configure Output Pin ¶ Assign an automatic function to a dedicated output, or return it to manual control. These functions follow the firmware’s motor-motion state for both command-driven and input-triggered moves. They are not measurements of encoder-confirmed belt motion. Usage ¶ M333 M333 P<pin> M333 P<pin> F<function> V<value> Use output indices 0 ? 3 . Without options, read all outputs; with P<pin> alone, read one. Parameter order is flexible. Function Activation condition F0 Manual output controlled with M330 . F1 The controller’s position-reached flag is set after a completed position move or an already-reached M312 target. This is a maintained state, not a timed pulse. F2 V0 The nonzero requested velocity is reached during a velocity run. Does not activate for position moves or a zero-speed target. F2 V>0 Signed motor speed is greater than or equal to the positive forward threshold in mm/s. F2 V<0 Signed motor speed is less than or equal to the negative reverse threshold in mm/s. Signed threshold functions can operate during either velocity or position moves. A new move or a change of motion mode clears the position-reached flag. Example ¶ M333 P0 F1 V0 M333 P1 F2 V50 M333 P2 F2 V-50 Each setting returns Ok and is saved to nonvolatile memory. Assigning a function initially turns the output off; the next control update applies its activation condition. While F1 / F2 is assigned, manual M330 requests are rejected. Use M333 P0 F0 to return Output 1 to manual control. Example response to M333 P1 ¶ O1 F2 V50.00 Queries use the prefix O in their responses, even though the command selects the pin with P . The all-output query returns O0 through O3 , with no trailing Ok . M389 - Enable Ethernet ¶ Set the Ethernet startup-enable flag and save the current Ethernet configuration immediately . Usage ¶ M389 <enable> 1 : enable Ethernet at startup and initialize it immediately with the current configuration. 0 : disable Ethernet at the next startup. In firmware 2.1.1, this does not close an already running server or TCP client connection. Response: Ok . Initialization status and the assigned IP address are also printed on the serial connection when enabling Ethernet. M390 - Set Ethernet Port ¶ Set the TCP server port in the current configuration. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M390 <port> Example ¶ M390 8844 Response: Ok . Startup uses the stored port; M397 shows the current configured value. M399 restores the port to 8844 . M391 - Set Ethernet IP Address ¶ Set the configured IPv4 address using four decimal octets. 0 0 0 0 selects DHCP when Ethernet is next initialized. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M391 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Static-IP example ¶ M391 192 168 0 2 DHCP ¶ M391 0 0 0 0 Each command returns Ok . M392 - Set Ethernet DNS Address ¶ Set the configured DNS address using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M392 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example ¶ M392 192 168 0 1 Response: Ok . M393 - Set Ethernet Gateway Address ¶ Set the configured gateway using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M393 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example ¶ M393 192 168 0 1 Response: Ok . M394 - Set Ethernet Subnet Address ¶ Set the configured subnet mask using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M394 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example ¶ M394 255 255 255 0 Response: Ok . M395 - Set Ethernet MAC Address ¶ Set the MAC address using six decimal byte values from 0 to 255 , separated by spaces. Convert a hexadecimal MAC address to decimal before sending it. Save and apply with M396 . Usage ¶ M395 <byte1> <byte2> <byte3> <byte4> <byte5> <byte6> Example ¶ M395 18 52 86 120 171 5 This represents 12:34:56:78:AB:05 . Response: Ok . M396 - Save and Init Ethernet Port ¶ Save the current Ethernet settings and enable flag to nonvolatile memory, then initialize the server with those settings. Usage ¶ M396 Configure network settings through serial, since applying them can interrupt the TCP connection. This command initializes Ethernet even if its startup-enable flag is 0 ; it does not change that flag. Use M389 1 when Ethernet should also start automatically after a restart. Response: Ok . Initialization status and the assigned IP address are also printed on the serial connection. M397 - Get Ethernet Port Parameters ¶ Read the configured values held by the firmware. These may include changes that have not yet been saved or applied. Usage ¶ M397 Example response ¶ E_port:8844 E_ip:192.168.0.2 E_dns:192.168.0.1 E_gateway:192.168.0.1 E_subnet:255.255.255.0 E_mac:18.52.86.120.171.5 The MAC address is reported as decimal bytes separated by dots. There is no trailing Ok . M398 - Get Ethernet Local Port Parameters ¶ Read the network stack’s active IP, DNS, gateway, and subnet . The port and MAC fields come from the firmware’s current configured values. Usage ¶ M398 The response uses the same fields as M397 , without a trailing Ok . After DHCP initialization, M397 can show the configured IP as 0.0.0.0 , while M398 shows the assigned IP. The text command IP returns the same information over both serial and TCP, without an extra echo line. M399 - Reset Ethernet Parameters ¶ Restore the following network configuration, save it to nonvolatile memory, and immediately reinitialize Ethernet: Setting Reset value TCP port 8844 Configured IP 0.0.0.0 (DHCP) Configured DNS, gateway, subnet 0.0.0.0 MAC address DE:AD:BE:EF:FE:32 (decimal bytes 222.173.190.239.254.50 ) This command leaves the Ethernet startup-enable flag unchanged. It resets network settings only, not motor, encoder, or I/O configuration. Use the serial connection because the active TCP connection can be interrupted. Usage ¶ M399 Configuration response ¶ E_port:8844 E_ip:0.0.0.0 E_dns:0.0.0.0 E_gateway:0.0.0.0 E_subnet:0.0.0.0 E_mac:222.173.190.239.254.50 There is no trailing Ok . Initialization status is also printed on serial. Use M398 or IP afterward to read the active address assigned by DHCP. XEncoder ¶ Encoder position, pulse calibration, and channel input commands. When updating an earlier X Encoder integration: Position reports use P0:<position> , rather than the P:<position> examples in the old reference. Read or set encoder calibration with M318 ; do not assume the old reference’s 5.12 pulses/mm value applies to the current controller. For M319 , select M316 2 and specify channel 0 (A) or 1 (B), such as M319 V0 or M319 T1 . These channels replace encoder pulse decoding while used as inputs. The controller’s separate digital inputs use M331 . M316 - Set Encoder Mode ¶ Select how encoder channels A and B are used. Setting a mode clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Usage ¶ M316 <mode> Mode Function 0 Absolute encoder position since the last reset. 1 Relative position change since the previous position report. 2 Digital input mode for channels A/B, queried with M319 . 3 Button mode on channels A/B. Motion control also requires M310 3 . Encoder-button behavior in mode 3 ¶ The firmware treats a channel’s HIGH logic state as pressed: Channel A active for more than 150 ms increases the button-speed target by 5 mm/s. Held for more than 2 seconds, it sets the target to the start speed configured by M315 B . Channel B active for more than 150 ms decreases the button-speed target by 5 mm/s. Held for more than 2 seconds, it requests zero speed. These button actions request velocity changes and do not interrupt an active position move. Use a dedicated input with M332 F4 to stop either type of motion in input mode. Button mode replaces encoder pulse decoding. It is separate from the four dedicated input functions configured with M332 . Example ¶ M316 1 Response: Ok . M317 - Get Position from Encoder ¶ Read the position once, configure periodic position reports, or reset the encoder position. Use one option per command. Usage ¶ M317 M317 T<period_ms> M317 R Option Function No option Return one position report. T<value> Set the report period in milliseconds. Values from 50 to 65535 enable reporting; values below 50 , including 0 , stop it. R Reset the encoder position to zero. This does not reset the motor position used by M312 . Position values use the absolute or relative mode selected by M316 and have two decimal places. Query ¶ M317 Example response: P0:5.32 Enable periodic reports ¶ M317 T500 The command returns Ok , followed by P0:<position> reports every 500 ms. Send M317 T0 to stop reporting. Reset ¶ M317 R Response: Ok . M318 - Set Encoder Parameters ¶ Read the encoder configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage ¶ M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale> Option Function No option Read encoder mode, scale, pulses/mm, reversal, and report period. S<value> Set the calibrated pulses/mm for the selected scale. Use a positive value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. C<value> Select pulse-counting scale: 1 , 2 , or 4 . Each valid setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Changing C does not automatically adjust S ; set both in separate commands. Calibration is loaded from nonvolatile memory, so this reference does not assume a fixed factory pulses/mm value. Example ¶ M318 C2 M318 S10.24 M318 R1 Each setting returns Ok . The pulses/mm value above is an example calibration for scale 2 . Example response to M318 ¶ M:1 C:2 S:10.24 R:1 T:500 M319 - Read Encoder Pin ¶ Read channels A/B as digital inputs, or report changes to their states. Select input-pin mode with M316 2 first; these functions replace normal encoder pulse decoding. Usage ¶ M319 V<pin> M319 T<pin> M319 S<pin> Option Function V<pin> Read the current input state. T<pin> Enable reports when the input state changes. S<pin> Disable reports when the input state changes. Pin 0 is encoder channel A; pin 1 is channel B. Send one option per command. T and S return Ok ; V returns the pin state without a trailing Ok . Example ¶ M319 V1 Example response: I1 V1 Reports use I0 V<state> or I1 V<state> , where state is 0 or 1 . Contact Us ¶ Store: https://deltaxstore.com Website: https://www.deltaxrobot.com Email: deltaxrobot@gmail.com Phone: +84 38 875 2005

docs.text: Use 115200 baud, 8N1 for the serial connection, or TCP to the configured Ethernet IP address and port. Send one command per line, terminated by LF ( \n ). CRLF is also accepted. Command names and parameter letters are case-sensitive. Separate parameters with spaces. Angle brackets in usage descriptions are placeholders; do not send the brackets. M315 , M317 , M318 , M319 , and M331 process only the first option on a line. Send separate commands for several settings. M332 and M333 accept their pin, function, and value together. Most setting commands return Ok . Queries return data without a trailing Ok . M312 returns Ok when the position move finishes rather than immediately. Wait for the expected response before sending the next command. Position moves are not queued. Automatic position or input reports can arrive between command responses. Serial lines are limited to 128 printable characters . An oversized line is discarded and returns Unknown:UART line too long! . Unrecognized M-codes return Unknown:Gcode! . Examples show commands and responses separately. Response values are illustrative except for the stated firmware/mainboard versions and date.

docs.text: M310 <mode> Mode Function 0 Output-pin mode. Control motor PUL/DIR/EN directly with M314 . 1 Position mode. Use M312 to move and M313 to set the move speed. 2 Velocity mode. Use M311 to set speed and direction. 3 Input-control mode. Functions assigned with M332 can change speed, move a relative distance, or stop. Resending the mode already active does not reset the motor position. The mode is saved to nonvolatile memory. Input mode also accepts M311 , subject to its motion-state restrictions. It is not potentiometer mode.

docs.text: Encoder position, pulse calibration, and channel input commands. When updating an earlier X Encoder integration: Position reports use P0:<position> , rather than the P:<position> examples in the old reference. Read or set encoder calibration with M318 ; do not assume the old reference’s 5.12 pulses/mm value applies to the current controller. For M319 , select M316 2 and specify channel 0 (A) or 1 (B), such as M319 V0 or M319 T1 . These channels replace encoder pulse decoding while used as inputs. The controller’s separate digital inputs use M331 .
docs.title: XEncoder

docs.text: Select how encoder channels A and B are used. Setting a mode clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration.
docs.title: M316 - Set Encoder Mode

docs.text: M316 <mode> Mode Function 0 Absolute encoder position since the last reset. 1 Relative position change since the previous position report. 2 Digital input mode for channels A/B, queried with M319 . 3 Button mode on channels A/B. Motion control also requires M310 3 .
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: The firmware treats a channel’s HIGH logic state as pressed: Channel A active for more than 150 ms increases the button-speed target by 5 mm/s. Held for more than 2 seconds, it sets the target to the start speed configured by M315 B . Channel B active for more than 150 ms decreases the button-speed target by 5 mm/s. Held for more than 2 seconds, it requests zero speed. These button actions request velocity changes and do not interrupt an active position move. Use a dedicated input with M332 F4 to stop either type of motion in input mode. Button mode replaces encoder pulse decoding. It is separate from the four dedicated input functions configured with M332 .

docs.title: M317 - Get Position from Encoder

docs.text: M317 M317 T<period_ms> M317 R Option Function No option Return one position report. T<value> Set the report period in milliseconds. Values from 50 to 65535 enable reporting; values below 50 , including 0 , stop it. R Reset the encoder position to zero. This does not reset the motor position used by M312 . Position values use the absolute or relative mode selected by M316 and have two decimal places.

docs.text: M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale> Option Function No option Read encoder mode, scale, pulses/mm, reversal, and report period. S<value> Set the calibrated pulses/mm for the selected scale. Use a positive value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. C<value> Select pulse-counting scale: 1 , 2 , or 4 . Each valid setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Changing C does not automatically adjust S ; set both in separate commands. docs.text: GCODES FOR SHORT CONVEYOR ¶ Communication and Responses ¶ Connect at 115200 baud , with 8 data bits, no parity, and 1 stop bit . Send one command per line, ending with a newline ( \n ) . CRLF is also accepted for the numeric commands below. Use uppercase command names, starting at the beginning of the line, followed by a space and a numeric value: M311 50 . Values are positional: use M311 50 , not M311 S50 . These commands are setters, not queries; always provide a value. Missing or nonnumeric values can be parsed as zero. The controller prints Begin: at startup and starts in potentiometer mode . The knob can therefore start the belt after power-on or reset. M310 , M311 , and M313 reply with Ok immediately. A nonzero M312 normally replies with Ok when its move completes. Settings are held in RAM and return to startup defaults after a reset. There is no save-to-memory command. This firmware implements M310, M311, M312, and M313 only . It does not implement IsXConveyor , encoder feedback, general-purpose input/output commands, or Ethernet commands. Unsupported commands do not produce an error reply. Quick Start ¶ Send each line separately and wait for its Ok reply before continuing. Select serial control: text M310 1 Run continuously at 50 mm/s: text M311 50 Stop continuous motion: text M311 0 For a relative position move, set the position speed with M313 , then send M312 and wait for its completion reply. M310 - Select Control Mode ¶ Select whether the potentiometer or serial commands control the conveyor. Usage ¶ M310 <mode> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description 0 Potentiometer mode, the startup default. The knob controls speed from 0 to 200 mm/s in one direction. 1 Serial mode. Use M311 for continuous motion and M312 for relative moves. The potentiometer is ignored in serial mode. Selecting serial mode sets the continuous speed request to zero; it does not clear an active position move. Select M310 1 before sending serial movement commands. In potentiometer mode, those commands do not immediately drive the motor, even when a command returns Ok . Example ¶ M310 1 Response: Ok . Switch modes only after a position move has completed. Returning to M310 0 lets the current knob setting control the belt again. M311 - Set Continuous Speed ¶ Run continuously at a signed speed, or stop continuous motion. Requires serial mode ( M310 1 ). Usage ¶ M311 <speed> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description <speed> Speed in mm/s. Positive and negative values select opposite directions. 0 stops continuous motion. The firmware limits the speed magnitude to 200 mm/s . A magnitude below 0.01 mm/s is treated as zero. It changes the step timing directly, without an acceleration ramp. Examples ¶ Run at 50 mm/s: M311 50 Run in the opposite direction: M311 -50 Stop continuous motion: M311 0 Each command replies with Ok . This acknowledges the command; it is not measured speed feedback. M311 0 does not cancel an active M312 position move. Wait for that move to finish before using continuous-speed commands. M312 - Move Relative Distance ¶ Move a signed distance from the current belt position, then stop. Requires serial mode ( M310 1 ). Set the movement speed with M313 . Usage ¶ M312 <distance> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description <distance> Relative distance in mm. Positive and negative values select opposite directions. This is not an absolute position or a homing command. The firmware converts distance to steps using 84 steps/mm , rounded to the nearest whole step. Position is calculated from commanded motor steps; there is no encoder verification. Direction convention In this firmware, positive M312 moves in the opposite direction to positive M311 . Negative values also have opposite direction conventions between the two commands. Example ¶ From a stopped conveyor in serial mode, set a position speed of 30 mm/s and wait for Ok : M313 30 Move 100 mm and wait for the completion Ok : M312 100 Move 100 mm in the opposite direction: M312 -100 Completion and Sequencing ¶ For a nonzero move, Ok is sent when the requested step count completes. The firmware then stops the step timer and disables the motor driver. M312 0 returns Ok immediately, but does not cancel a move that is already running. There is no motion queue or position-move cancellation command. Wait for completion before sending another motion, mode, or position-speed command; commands sent during a move can modify its active step count, direction, or speed. Very small nonzero distances can round to zero steps and produce no completion reply . One step is approximately 0.0119 mm ; use distances of at least one step for normal positioning. M313 - Set Position Move Speed ¶ Set the speed used by M312 . The startup default is 30 mm/s . Configure this while the conveyor is stopped, before starting a position move. Usage ¶ M313 <speed> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description <speed> Positive position-move speed in mm/s. Use a value no greater than 200 mm/s. Direction is selected by the sign of M312 , not by this value. The firmware assigns this value directly: it does not validate or clamp M313 like it does M311 . Do not use zero or negative values. This setting is lost after reset. Example ¶ M313 40 Response: Ok . Subsequent M312 moves use 40 mm/s. M313 does not specify a distance and does not start a move from idle. Related Documentation ¶ Short Conveyor specifications Firmware source: command parser and motor control

docs.text: Gcodes for Delta X 1 ¶ G00, G01 - Linear Move ¶ Descriptions ¶ The G0 and G1 commands add a LINEAR MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set the feed rate with F once. Subsequent movement commands use that feed rate until you change it; you do not need to repeat F in every movement command. Usage ¶ G00 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] G01 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. Example ¶ G01 X12 ;move to 12mm on the X-axis G01 F200 ;set the feedrate to 200 mm/s G01 X90.6 Y13.8 ;move to 90.6mm on the X-axis and 13.8mm on the Y-axis G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G01 W90 ;rotate to 90 degree on the 4-axis G01 X100 Y50 Z-400 W90 U45 F200 ;X=100 mm, Y=50 mm, Z=-400 mm, W=90°, U=45°, F=200 mm/s G02, G03 - Arc or Circle Move ¶ Descriptions ¶ G2 adds a clockwise arc move to the planner; G3 adds a counter-clockwise arc. An arc move starts at the current position and ends at the given XYZ, pivoting around a center-point offset given by I and J. Usage ¶ G2 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] G3 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. I[offset] (mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] (mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. Example ¶ G28 G01 Z-350 G01 X50 G02 X-50 Y0 I-50 J0 G03 X50 Y0 I50 J0 G04 - Dwell/Delay ¶ Descriptions ¶ Dwell pauses the command queue and waits for a period of time. Usage ¶ G04 [P<time>] Parameters ¶ P[time]: delay time in miliseconds. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X100 G05 - Bézier cubic spline ¶ Descriptions ¶ G5 creates a cubic B-spline in the XY plane with the X and Y axes only. P and Q parameters are required . I and J are required for the first G5 command in a series . For subsequent G5 commands, either both I and J must be specified , or neither. Usage ¶ G5 [F<rate>] I<pos> J<pos> P<pos> Q<pos> X<pos> Y<pos> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum feedrate of the move between the start and end point. This value applies to all subsequent moves. I[offset] (mm) Offset from the X start point to first control point. J[offset] (mm) Offset from the Y start point to first control point. P[offset] (mm) Offset from the X end point to second control point. Q[offset] (mm) Offset from the Y end point to the second control point. X[pos] (mm) A destination coordinate on the X axis. Y[pos] (mm) A destination coordinate on the Y axis. Example ¶ ;program a curvy “N” shape G0 X0 Y0 G5 I0 J3 P0 Q-3 X1 Y1 G06 - Theta angle control ¶ Descriptions ¶ Directly control movement angle without endpoint coordinates. Usage ¶ G06 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [P<pos>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. X[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. P[pos] (mm) Distance traveled. Example ¶ G6 X0 Y0 Z0 ;set theta 1, theta 2, theta 3 angle at 0 deg G28 - Homing ¶ Descriptions ¶ Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage ¶ G28 G90 - Absolute Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage ¶ G90 Note Absolute positioning is the default. G91 - Relative Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage ¶ G91 Example ¶ G91 ; Set all axes to relative M03, M04 - Ouput On / Laser On / Vacuum On / Gripper Close ¶ Descriptions ¶ M03 is used to turn on the vacuum pump, laser, and close the gripper. Usage ¶ M03 [S<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] Vacuum pump (empty), Spindle speed (0 - 255), laser power (0 - 255), angle of gripper (0-100), if value is emtpy then gripper close. Note: M03 will be equivalent to M03 S255. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 M03 ;turn on Vacuum pump G01 Z-300 M05 - Ouput Off / Laser Off / Vacuum Off / Gripper Open ¶ Descriptions ¶ M05 is used to turn off the vacuum pump, laser, or close the gripper. Usage ¶ M05 M84 - Disable Steppers ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command can be used to disable steppers. Usage ¶ M84 M104 - Set Hotend Temperature ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set a new target hot end temperature and continue without waiting. The firmware will continue to try to reach and hold the temperature in the background. Usage ¶ M104 [S<temp>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[temp] (degree Celsius) Target temperature. Example ¶ M104 S295 ;set hotend at 295 degC M109 - Wait For Hotend Temperature ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command optionally sets a new target hot end temperature and waits for the target temperature to be reached before proceeding. Usage ¶ M109 [S<temp>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[temp] (degree Celsius) Target temperature. Example ¶ M109 S180 ;Set target temperature and wait (if heating up) M203 - Set Max Feedrate ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement max feedrate. Usage ¶ M203 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] (mm/s) max feedrate. Example ¶ M203 S500 ;Set max feedrate M204 - Set Acceleration ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement acceleration. Usage ¶ M204 A<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description A[value] (mm/s2) end effector acceleration. Example ¶ M204 A5000 ;Set max feedrate M206 - Set Z Offset ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set z home offset. Usage ¶ M206 Z<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description Z[value] (mm) offset value. Example ¶ M206 Z30 ;Set z home offset M360 - Select End Effector ¶ Descriptions ¶ Select the end effector for the robot. You can change the end effector to one of these : Vacuum, gripper, pen, laser, printer or use your custom end effector. Usage ¶ M360 E<value> Parameters ¶ E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen 3-Laser 4-Printer 5-Custom Example ¶ M360 E2 ;select the end effector is Pen M361 - Set Interpolated line length ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the length of each segment in line interpolation. Usage ¶ M361 P<len> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Length in mm. Example ¶ M361 P0.3 ;set segment length = 0.3mm M362 - Set Arc segment length ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set segment length in arc interpolation. Usage ¶ M362 P<len> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Length in mm. Example ¶ M362 P0.4 ;set segment length = 0.4mm M500 - Save Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Save all configurable settings to EEPROM. Usage ¶ M500 Example ¶ M500 ;Save settings M501 - Restore Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Load all saved settings from EEPROM. Usage ¶ M501 Example ¶ M501 ;Restore all settings. M502 - Reset Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Reset all configurable settings to their factory defaults. Usage ¶ M502 Example ¶ M502 ;reset Contact Us ¶ Store: https://deltaxstore.com Website: https://www.deltaxrobot.com Email: deltaxrobot@gmail.com Phone: +84 38 875 2005

docs.text: Gcodes for Delta X 2 ¶ G00, G01 - Linear Move ¶ Descriptions ¶ The G0 and G1 commands add a LINEAR MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set the feed rate with F once. Subsequent movement commands use that feed rate until you change it; you do not need to repeat F in every movement command. Usage ¶ G00 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] G01 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. Example ¶ G01 X12 ;move to 12mm on the X-axis G01 F200 ;set the feedrate to 200 mm/s G01 X90.6 Y13.8 ;move to 90.6mm on the X-axis and 13.8mm on the Y-axis G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G01 W90 ;rotate to 90 degree on the 4-axis G01 X100 Y50 Z-400 W90 U45 F200 ;X=100 mm, Y=50 mm, Z=-400 mm, W=90°, U=45°, F=200 mm/s G02, G03 - Arc or Circle Move ¶ Descriptions ¶ G2 adds a clockwise arc move to the planner; G3 adds a counter-clockwise arc. An arc move starts at the current position and ends at the given XYZ, pivoting around a center-point offset given by I and J. Usage ¶ G2 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] G3 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. I[offset] (mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] (mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. Example ¶ G28 G01 Z-350 G01 X50 G02 X-50 Y0 I-50 J0 G03 X50 Y0 I50 J0 G04 - Dwell/Delay ¶ Descriptions ¶ Dwell pauses the command queue and waits for a period of time. Usage ¶ G04 [P<time>] Parameters ¶ P[time]: delay time in miliseconds. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X100 G05 - Bézier cubic spline ¶ Descriptions ¶ G5 creates a cubic B-spline in the XY plane with the X and Y axes only. P and Q parameters are required . I and J are required for the first G5 command in a series . For subsequent G5 commands, either both I and J must be specified , or neither. Usage ¶ G5 [F<rate>] I<pos> J<pos> P<pos> Q<pos> X<pos> Y<pos> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum feedrate of the move between the start and end point. This value applies to all subsequent moves. I[offset] (mm) Offset from the X start point to first control point. J[offset] (mm) Offset from the Y start point to first control point. P[offset] (mm) Offset from the X end point to second control point. Q[offset] (mm) Offset from the Y end point to the second control point. X[pos] (mm) A destination coordinate on the X axis. Y[pos] (mm) A destination coordinate on the Y axis. Example ¶ ;program a curvy “N” shape G0 X0 Y0 G5 I0 J3 P0 Q-3 X1 Y1 G06 - Theta angle control ¶ Descriptions ¶ Directly control movement angle without endpoint coordinates. Usage ¶ G06 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [P<pos>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. X[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. P[pos] (mm) Distance traveled. Example ¶ G6 X0 Y0 Z0 ;set theta 1, theta 2, theta 3 angle at 0 deg G28 - Homing ¶ Descriptions ¶ Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage ¶ G28 G90 - Absolute Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage ¶ G90 Note Absolute positioning is the default. G91 - Relative Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage ¶ G91 Example ¶ G91 ; Set all axes to relative G93 - Get Current Position ¶ Descriptions ¶ Get current posiition of end effector. Usage ¶ G93 Feedback ¶ <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> <xpos> : Current X position. <ypos> : Current Y position. <zpos> : Current Z position. Example ¶ G93 ; get current pos return: 31, 43, -270 M03, M04 - Ouput On / Laser On / Vacuum On / Gripper Close ¶ Descriptions ¶ M03 is used to turn on the vacuum pump, laser, and close the gripper. Usage ¶ M03 [S<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] Vacuum pump (empty), Spindle speed (0 - 255), laser power (0 - 255), angle of gripper (0-100), if value is emtpy then gripper close. Note: M03 will be equivalent to M03 S255. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 M03 ;turn on Vacuum pump G01 Z-300 M05 - Ouput Off / Laser Off / Vacuum Off / Gripper Open ¶ Descriptions ¶ M05 is used to turn off the vacuum pump, laser, or close the gripper. Usage ¶ M05 M84 - Disable Steppers ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command can be used to disable steppers. Usage ¶ M84 M104 - Set Hotend Temperature ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set a new target hot end temperature and continue without waiting. The firmware will continue to try to reach and hold the temperature in the background. Usage ¶ M104 [S<temp>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[temp] (degree Celsius) Target temperature. Example ¶ M104 S195 ;set hotend at 195 degC M105 - Report Temperature ¶ Descriptions ¶ Request a temperature report to be sent to the host as soon as possible. Usage ¶ M105 Example ¶ M105 ;set hotend at 95 degC return T:195 M109 - Wait For Hotend Temperature ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command optionally sets a new target hot end temperature and waits for the target temperature to be reached before proceeding. Usage ¶ M109 [S<temp>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[temp] (degree Celsius) Target temperature. Example ¶ M109 S180 ;Set target temperature and wait (if heating up) M203 - Set Feedrate ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement feedrate. Usage ¶ M203 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] (mm/s) max feedrate. Example ¶ M203 S500 ;Set max feedrate M204 - Set Acceleration ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement acceleration. Usage ¶ M204 A<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description A[value] (mm/s2) end effector acceleration. Example ¶ M204 A5000 ;Set movement acceleration. M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set segment begin/end velocity. Usage ¶ M205 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] (mm/s2) end effector begin/end velocity. Example ¶ M205 S40 ;Set begin speed at 40 mm/s M206 - Set Axis Offset ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set home offset for one or all axis. Usage ¶ M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[value] (mm) X offset value. Y[value] (mm) Y offset value. Z[value] (mm) Z offset value. Example ¶ M206 X20 Y-10 Z30 ;Set home offsets M331 - Select Linked Device ¶ Descriptions ¶ Config device is linked to external UART port. Usage ¶ M331 R<value> Parameters ¶ R[value] 0-None (Disable port). 1-Conveyor 2-Sliding Rail Example ¶ M331 R1 ;select the device which connected with external port is Conveyor, now you can control Conveyor via Delta Robot M360 - Select End Effector ¶ Descriptions ¶ Select the end effector for the robot. You can change the end effector to one of these : Vacuum, gripper, pen, laser, printer or use your custom end effector. Usage ¶ M360 E<value> Parameters ¶ E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen 3-Laser 4-Printer 5-Custom Example ¶ M360 E2 ;select the end effector is Pen M361 - Set Interpolated line length ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the length of each segment in line interpolation. Usage ¶ M361 P<len> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Length in mm. Example ¶ M361 P0.3 ;set segment length = 0.3mm M362 - Set Arc segment length ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set segment length in arc interpolation. Usage ¶ M362 P<len> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Length in mm. Example ¶ M362 P0.4 ;set segment length = 0.4mm M402 - Set Z Max Position ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the maximum position of Z axis, the end effector can’t move upper than this value. Usage ¶ M402 Z<pos> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description Z[pos] (mm) max z position in mm. Example ¶ M402 Z-245 ;After this command, end effector cant get higher than -245 mm. M500 - Save Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Save all configurable settings to EEPROM. Usage ¶ M500 Example ¶ M500 ;Save settings M501 - Restore Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Load all saved settings from EEPROM. Usage ¶ M501 Example ¶ M501 ;Restore all settings. M502 - Reset Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Reset all configurable settings to their factory defaults. Usage ¶ M502 Example ¶ M502 ;reset Contact Us ¶ Store: https://deltaxstore.com Website: https://www.deltaxrobot.com Email: deltaxrobot@gmail.com Phone: +84 38 875 2005

docs.text: Gcodes for Delta X 2 ¶ G00, G01 - Linear Move ¶ Descriptions ¶ The G0 and G1 commands add a LINEAR MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage ¶ G00 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] G01 [F<rate>] [A<rate>] [J<rate>] [S<rate>] [E<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[rate] (mm/s^2) The maximum acceleration of the movement. J[rate] (mm/s^3) The jerk of the movement. S[rate] (mm/s) The start velocity of the movement. E[rate] (mm/s) The end velocity of the movement. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. U[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 5-axis. Example ¶ G01 X12 ;move to 12mm on the X-axis G01 F200 ;set the feedrate to 200 mm/s G01 X90.6 Y13.8 ;move to 90.6mm on the X-axis and 13.8mm on the Y-axis G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G01 W90 ;rotate to 90 degree on the 4-axis G01 X100 Y50 Z-400 W90 U45 F200 ;X=100 mm, Y=50 mm, Z=-400 mm, W=90°, U=45°, F=200 mm/s G02, G03 - Arc or Circle Move ¶ Descriptions ¶ G2 adds a clockwise arc move to the planner; G3 adds a counter-clockwise arc. An arc move starts at the current position and ends at the given XYZ, pivoting around a center-point offset given by I and J. Usage ¶ G2 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] G3 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. I[offset] (mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] (mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. U[angle] (mm) A coordinate on the 5-axis. Example ¶ G28 G01 Z-350 G01 X50 G02 X-50 Y0 I-50 J0 G03 X50 Y0 I50 J0 G04 - Dwell/Delay ¶ Descriptions ¶ Dwell pauses the command queue and waits for a period of time. Usage ¶ G04 [P<time>] Parameters ¶ P[time]: delay time in miliseconds. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X100 G05 - Bézier cubic spline ¶ Descriptions ¶ G5 creates a cubic B-spline in the XY plane with the X and Y axes only. P and Q parameters are required . I and J are required for the first G5 command in a series . For subsequent G5 commands, either both I and J must be specified , or neither. Usage ¶ G5 [F<rate>] I<pos> J<pos> P<pos> Q<pos> X<pos> Y<pos> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[rate] (mm/s) The maximum feedrate of the move between the start and end point. This value applies to all subsequent moves. I[offset] (mm) Offset from the X start point to first control point. J[offset] (mm) Offset from the Y start point to first control point. P[offset] (mm) Offset from the X end point to second control point. Q[offset] (mm) Offset from the Y end point to the second control point. X[pos] (mm) A destination coordinate on the X axis. Y[pos] (mm) A destination coordinate on the Y axis. Example ¶ ;program a curvy “N” shape G0 X0 Y0 G5 I0 J3 P0 Q-3 X1 Y1 G06 - Theta angle control ¶ Descriptions ¶ Directly control movement angle without endpoint coordinates. Usage ¶ G06 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. Example ¶ G6 X0 Y0 Z0 ;set theta 1, theta 2, theta 3 angle at 0 deg G28 - Homing ¶ Descriptions ¶ Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage ¶ G28 G90 - Absolute Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage ¶ G90 Note Absolute positioning is the default. G91 - Relative Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage ¶ G91 Example ¶ G91 ; Set all axes to relative G93 - Get Current Position ¶ Descriptions ¶ Get current position of end effector. Usage ¶ G93 Feedback ¶ <xpos>, <ypos>, <zpos> <xpos> : Current X position. <ypos> : Current Y position. <zpos> : Current Z position. Example ¶ G93 ; get current pos return: 31, 43, -270 M03 - Vacuum On / Gripper Close ¶ Descriptions ¶ M03 is used to turn on the vacuum pump or close the gripper. Usage ¶ M03 Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 M03 ;turn on Vacuum pump G01 Z-300 M04 - Turn on digital output pins ¶ Descriptions ¶ M04 is used to turn on and set PWM value for digital output pin (D0 - D3). Usage ¶ M04 [D<pin>] [P<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description D[pin] (0 ~ 3) The index of output pin P[value] (0 - 255) The value of the pwm Example ¶ M04 D1 P128 ;set pin D1 pwm at 50% M05 - Vacuum Off / Gripper Open ¶ Descriptions ¶ M05 is used to turn off the vacuum pump or close the gripper. Usage ¶ M05 ;turn off vacuum M06 - Turn off digital output pins ¶ Descriptions ¶ M06 is used to turn off digital output pin (D0 - D3). Usage ¶ M06 [D<pin>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description D[pin] (0 ~ 3) The index of output pin Example ¶ M06 D1 ;turn off pin D1 M07 - Read Input Signals ¶ Descriptions ¶ M07 is used to read the input signal from the input pins. Usage ¶ M07 [I<pin>] [A<pin>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description I[pin] (0 ~ 3) The index of digital input pin A[pin] (0 ~ 1) The index of analog input pin Feedback ¶ I[pin] V[value] : I[pin] : The index of digital input pin V[value] : {0,1} The value of the digital input signal A[pin] V[value] : A[pin] : The index of analog input pin V[value] : [0 ~ 4095] The value of the analog input signal Example ¶ M07 I0 I3 ;read digital pin I0 and I3 >>> I0 V1 >>> I3 V0 M07 A1 ;read analog pin A1 >>> A1 V3946 M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically ¶ Descriptions ¶ M08 is used to read the input signal from the input pins automatically. Usage ¶ M08 [I<pin>] M08 [A<pin>] [P<time>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description I[pin] (0 ~ 3) The index of digital input pin A[pin] (0 ~ 1) The index of analog input pin P[time] (ms) The time to read the analog input signal Feedback ¶ I[pin] V[value] : I[pin] : The index of digital input pin V[value] : {0,1} The value of the digital input signal A[pin] V[value] : A[pin] : The index of analog input pin V[value] : [0 ~ 4095] The value of the analog input signal Example ¶ M08 I0 ;read digital pin I0 automatically M08 A1 P1000 ;read analog pin A1 every 1000ms M09 - Disable Automatic Reading Analog Input Signal ¶ Descriptions ¶ M09 is used to disable automatic reading the analog input signal. Usage ¶ M09 [A<pin>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description A[pin] (0 ~ 1) The index of analog input pin Example ¶ M09 A1 ;disable automatic reading analog pin A1 M50 - Enable RJ45 ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command can be used to enable or disable RJ45 port. Usage ¶ M50 A<x> Parameter ¶ A[x] x = 1 : enable RJ45 x = 0 : disable RJ45 Example ¶ M50 A1 ; enable RJ45 M51 - Set Ethernet Port ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set ethernet port number Usage ¶ M51 B<x> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description B[x] port number Example ¶ M51 B8080 ; set ethernet port M52 - Set MAC Device ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set MAC address of the robot Usage ¶ Address form: A:B:C:D:E:F M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number E[u] number F[v] number Example ¶ M52 A12 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 >>> MAC add: 12-23-34-45-56-67 M53 - Set Ethernet IP ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set ethernet IP of robot Usage ¶ M53 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M53 A192 B168 C1 D1 >>> IP: 192.168.1.1 M54 - Set Ethernet DNS ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set ethernet DNS address Usage ¶ M54 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M53 A192 B168 C1 D3 >>> DNS IP: 192.168.1.3 M55 - Set Ethernet Gateway ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set ethernet gateway address Usage ¶ M55 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ ; set ethernet gateway address 192.168.3.1 M55 A192 B168 C3 D1 M56 - Set Ethernet Subnet ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set ethernet gateway address Usage ¶ M56 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ ; set ethernet subnet address 192.168.3.1 M56 A192 B168 C3 D1 M57 - Get Robot IP ¶ Descriptions ¶ Get the IP of Delta X 2 Plus Robot Usage ¶ M57 Example ¶ M57 >>> 192.168.2.2 M84 - Disable Steppers ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command can be used to disable steppers. Usage ¶ M84 M203 - Set Feedrate ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement feedrate. Usage ¶ M203 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] (mm/s) max feedrate. Example ¶ M203 S500 ;Set max feedrate M204 - Set Acceleration ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement acceleration. Usage ¶ M204 A<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description A[value] (mm/s2) end effector acceleration. Example ¶ M204 A5000 ;Set movement acceleration. M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set segment begin/end velocity. Usage ¶ M205 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] (mm/s2) end effector begin/end velocity. Example ¶ M205 S40 ;Set begin speed at 40 mm/s M206 - Set Axis Offset ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set home offset for one or all axis. Usage ¶ M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[value] (mm) X offset value. Y[value] (mm) Y offset value. Z[value] (mm) Z offset value. Example ¶ M206 X20 Y-10 Z30 ;Set home offsets M207 - Set Z Safe ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the lowest Z level that the robot cannot exceed. Usage ¶ M207 [Z<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description Z[value] (mm) Z safe value. Example ¶ M207 Z-870 ;Set Z safe value M210 - Set Theta Movement Parameter ¶ Descriptions ¶ Config theta movement para like speed, accel, jerk, start velocity and end velocity. Usage ¶ M210 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[value] (unit/s) speed. A[value] (unit/s^2) accel. J[value] (unit/s^3) jerk. S[value] (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] (unit/s) end velocity. Example ¶ M210 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;set all theta movement para M360 - Select End Effector ¶ Descriptions ¶ Select the end effector for the robot. You can change the end effector to one of these : Vacuum, gripper, pen, laser, printer or use your custom end effector. Usage ¶ M360 E<value> Parameters ¶ E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen 3-Laser 4-Printer 5-Custom Example ¶ M360 E2 ;select the end effector is Pen M361 - Set minimum moving distance ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the length of minimum moving distance. Usage ¶ M361 P<len> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Length in mm. Example ¶ M361 P0.1 ;set minium moving distance = 0.1mm M500 - Save Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Save all configurable settings to EEPROM. Usage ¶ M500 Example ¶ M500 ;Save settings M501 - Restore Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Load all saved settings from EEPROM. Usage ¶ M501 Example ¶ M501 ;Restore all settings. M502 - Reset Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Reset all configurable settings to their factory defaults. Usage ¶ M502 Example ¶ M502 ;reset Contact Us ¶ Store: https://deltaxstore.com Website: https://www.deltaxrobot.com Email: deltaxrobot@gmail.com Phone: +84 38 875 2005
