docs.text: G-CODES FOR DELTA X 3 ¶ G0, G1 - Linear Movement ¶ Descriptions ¶ The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Run G28 before the first XYZ move after startup, disabling the motors, or resetting/loading settings. Commands that only set motion parameters or move W/U do not require XYZ homing. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage ¶ G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (degrees) Axis W position, within the limits configured by M60 . U[angle] (degrees) Axis U position, within the limits configured by M61 . F[val] (mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] (mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] (mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Start and end velocities are limited to max(F - 2, 0) . The planner may reduce motion parameters to keep the XYZ step rates within their limits. When this happens, the robot reports Replace F<value> A<value> J<value> S<value> E<value> before Ok , with three decimal places. These are the effective settings for that move; the stored motion settings remain unchanged. Example ¶ G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to X0 Y0 Z-360 G01 X50 ;move to X50, keeping Y0 and Z-360 G01 W90 U45 ;rotate W to 90 degrees and U to 45 degrees G00 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;return to X0 Y0 Z-360 G01 W0 U0 ;return W and U to 0 degrees G2, G3 - Controlled Arc Movement ¶ Descriptions ¶ On Delta X 3, G2 moves counter-clockwise and G3 moves clockwise , viewed from +Z toward the XY plane. The arc starts at the current XY position and ends at the specified XY position, around the center defined by I and J. Z remains unchanged throughout the arc. Both I and J are required, including when either offset is zero. J specifies the arc center’s Y offset; the previously set jerk remains in use. Run G28 before XYZ motion. Endpoints follow G90 or G91 ; I/J are always offsets from the arc’s starting point. Usage ¶ G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description I[offset] (mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] (mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] (degrees) Axis W position, within the limits configured by M60 . U[angle] (degrees) Axis U position, within the limits configured by M61 . F[val] (mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] (mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. These motion settings remain in effect for subsequent moves until changed. Example ¶ G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X50 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the arc's starting point G02 X0 Y50 I-50 J0 ;move 90 degrees counter-clockwise around X0 Y0 G03 X50 Y0 I0 J-50 ;move 90 degrees clockwise back to X50 Y0 Both arcs have a 50 mm radius and a path length of approximately 78.54 mm. Z stays at -360 mm. G4 - Dwell/Delay ¶ Descriptions ¶ Pause the robot for a period of time. Usage ¶ G4 P<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[value] Required delay in milliseconds, integer from 0 to 4294967295. Example ¶ G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the starting position G04 P500 ;wait 500 ms (0.5 seconds) G01 X50 ;move 50 mm along X after the delay G6 - Theta angle control ¶ Descriptions ¶ Move the three upper arms to specified Theta angles. Run G28 first. G90 selects absolute joint angles; G91 selects relative angle changes. Motion settings use Cartesian units and remain in effect for subsequent moves until changed. Usage ¶ G6 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. F[val] (mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] (mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] (mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Example ¶ G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute joint angles G6 X0 Y0 Z0 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;move all three upper arms to 0 degrees G6 X10 Y10 Z10 ;move all three upper arms to 10 degrees G6 X0 Y0 Z0 ;return all three upper arms to 0 degrees With the standard X3 geometry, equal joint angles of 0 degrees place the tool at approximately X0 Y0 Z-360.46; equal angles of 10 degrees place it at approximately X0 Y0 Z-382.37 in the base coordinate system. G28 - Homing ¶ Descriptions ¶ Home the three XYZ motors using their home sensors and move the W and U servos to their configured home positions. W/U do not seek endstops. Homing establishes the XYZ position reference needed for movement and position queries. Usage ¶ G28 Example G28 ;home XYZ and move W/U to their configured home angles G90 - Absolute Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage ¶ G90 Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the starting position G01 X50 ;move to absolute X50 G01 X20 ;move back to absolute X20, a -30 mm change G91 - Relative Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage ¶ G91 Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the starting position G91 ;use relative positioning G01 X50 ;move +50 mm along X, ending at X50 G01 X-20 Y30 ;move -20 mm in X and +30 mm in Y, ending at X30 Y30 G90 ;restore absolute positioning G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;return to the starting position G93 - Get Current Position ¶ Descriptions ¶ Get the current XYZ position calculated from the motor steps already emitted. The response uses the robot’s base G-code coordinates, without the working origin set by M206 . Use PositionOffset for coordinates relative to that origin. Run G28 first. If the XYZ reference is unknown, the response is Error:XYZ position is unknown; home with G28. Usage ¶ G93 Feedback ¶ <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> : Coordinates in mm, with two decimal places. <xpos> : Current X position. <ypos> : Current Y position. <zpos> : Current Z position. Example ¶ G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the position to query G93 ;read the XYZ position in mm >>> 0.00,0.00,-360.00 The response is an example; the reported position can differ slightly from the target because it is calculated from emitted motor steps. M03, M04 - Output On / Set PWM / Vacuum On ¶ Descriptions ¶ Turn on a Delta X 3 digital output, set a PWM output, or control the end effector selected by M360 . Usage ¶ M03 D<x> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y> M03 S<value> Parameters ¶ M03 D[x] or M04 D[x] : Turn on a digital output. x = 0, 1, 2, 3 for the external digital outputs. x = 4 controls the selected end effector. With vacuum mode ( M360 E0 ), it turns the vacuum on. M03 P[x] W[y] : Set a PWM output. x = 0, 1. y = integer from 0 to 255; required. M04 P[x] W[y] : Set a PWM output with a larger value range. x = 0, 1. y = integer from 0 to 65535; required. M03 S[value] or M04 S[value] : Control the selected end effector, with an integer value from 0 to 100. Vacuum ( M360 E0 ): turns the vacuum on. Gripper ( M360 E1 ): positions the gripper within the range configured by M62 ; S0 is fully open and S100 is fully closed. Use separate commands for digital ( D ) and PWM ( P ) outputs. W is used only with PWM outputs. Example ¶ M03 D0 ;turn on digital output D0 M05 D0 ;turn off digital output D0 M03 P0 W128 ;set P0 to 128/255, approximately 50.20% PWM M05 P0 ;turn off PWM output P0 M04 P1 W32768 ;set P1 to 32768/65535, approximately 50.00% PWM M05 P1 ;turn off PWM output P1 M360 E0 ;select the vacuum M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum G04 P500 ;keep the vacuum on for 0.5 seconds M05 ;turn off the vacuum M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move halfway between the configured gripper angle limits G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper M05 - Output Off / Turn Off PWM / Vacuum Off ¶ Descriptions ¶ Turn off a Delta X 3 digital output, set a PWM output to zero, or turn off the selected end effector. Usage ¶ M05 M05 D<x> M05 P<x> Parameters ¶ M05 or M05 D4 : Turn off the end effector selected by M360 . In vacuum mode, turn off the vacuum; in gripper mode, open the gripper. M05 D[x] : turn off digital output pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. M05 P[x] : turn off PWM output pin x = 0, 1. Example ¶ M03 D0 ;turn on digital output D0 M05 D0 ;turn off digital output D0 M03 P0 W128 ;enable PWM output P0 M05 P0 ;set P0 PWM to zero M360 E0 ;select the vacuum M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum M05 ;turn off the selected vacuum M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move the gripper to the middle of its configured range M05 D4 ;open the selected gripper M07 - Read Input Signals. ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read Digital and Analog input signals. Usage ¶ M07 I<x> M07 A<x> Parameters ¶ M07 I[x] : Read Digital Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. M07 A[x] : Read Analog Input Pin x = 0, 1. Feedback ¶ I[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = [0, 1023] Example ¶ M07 I0 I3 ;read digital inputs I0 and I3 >>> I0 V1 >>> I3 V0 M07 A1 ;read analog input A1 on the 0-1023 scale >>> A1 V512 Input values shown are illustrative and depend on the connected signals. M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically. ¶ Descriptions ¶ Report digital input changes automatically, or report analog input values at a configured interval. Usage ¶ M08 I<x> B<y> M08 A<x> C<y> Parameters ¶ M08 I[x] B[y] : auto read digital input pins. I[x] : Digital Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. B[y] : Required digital reporting mode. y = 1 : Start the auto-reading digital input signal process. y = 0 : Stop the auto-reading digital input signal process. M08 A[x] C[y] A[x] : Analog Input Pin x = 0, 1. C[y] : Required nonnegative integer interval setting. y > 50 : Enable analog reporting, with an interval of floor(y / 10) milliseconds. For example, C200 sets a 20 ms interval and C5000 sets a 500 ms interval. y <= 50 : Disable analog reporting. Feedback ¶ I[x] V[val] : return auto read digital input value x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : return auto read analog input value x = pin number val = [0, 1023] Example ¶ M08 I3 B1 ;report each change of digital input I3 M08 A1 C5000 ;report analog input A1 every 500 ms (5000/10) >>> I3 V0 >>> A1 V512 M08 I3 B0 ;stop automatic reports from I3 M08 A1 C0 ;stop automatic reports from A1 Input values shown are illustrative and depend on the connected signals. M9 - Stop Analog Input Auto Feedback ¶ Descriptions ¶ Turn off auto feedback for an analog input pin. Usage ¶ M9 A<n> Parameters ¶ A[n] : Analog Input Pin n = 0, 1. Example ¶ M08 A1 C5000 ;enable A1 reports at a 500 ms interval G04 P1000 ;wait 1 second M9 A1 ;stop A1 analog reports M43 - Set UART2 / Serial2 ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure UART2 / Serial2. Use A1 to enable, A0 to disable, and B to set the baudrate. Both parameters are required, including when disabling the port. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied after the reply. Usage ¶ M43 A<x> B<y> Parameters ¶ A[x] x = 1 : enable UART2 / Serial2. x = 0 : disable UART2 / Serial2. B[y] : Baudrate, integer from 1200 to 3000000. Example ¶ M43 A1 B115200 ;enable UART2 / Serial2 at 115200 baud M43 A0 B115200 ;disable UART2 / Serial2 Send these configuration commands through USB so disabling UART2 does not interrupt your control connection. M44 - Set UART3 / Serial3 ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure UART3 / Serial3. Use A1 to enable, A0 to disable, and B to set the baudrate. Both parameters are required, including when disabling the port. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied after the reply. Usage ¶ M44 A<x> B<y> Parameters ¶ A[x] x = 1 : enable UART3 / Serial3. x = 0 : disable UART3 / Serial3. B[y] : Baudrate, integer from 1200 to 3000000. Example ¶ M44 A1 B115200 ;enable UART3 / Serial3 at 115200 baud M44 A0 B115200 ;disable UART3 / Serial3 Send these configuration commands through USB so disabling UART3 does not interrupt your control connection. M50 - Enable RJ45 ¶ Descriptions ¶ Enable or disable the RJ45 Ethernet port. The setting is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M50 A<x> Parameter ¶ A[x] x = 1 : enable RJ45 x = 0 : disable RJ45 Example ¶ M50 A1 ;enable the RJ45 Ethernet port >>> Ok The Ethernet examples use robot IP 192.168.1.100 , DNS/gateway 192.168.1.1 , subnet mask 255.255.255.0 , and TCP port 8844 . Configure the robot through USB; a computer on this subnet can use an unused address such as 192.168.1.10 . M51 - Set Ethernet Port ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet server port. The setting is saved to EEPROM and the server restarts with the new port. Usage ¶ M51 B<x> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description B[x] Port number, integer from 1 to 65535. Example ¶ M51 B8844 ;set the Ethernet TCP port to 8844 >>> Ok M52 - Set MAC Device ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the robot’s MAC address. All six decimal bytes are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ Address form: A:B:C:D:E:F M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number E[u] number F[v] number Example ¶ M52 A2 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 ;set MAC bytes to 2-23-34-45-56-67 (decimal) >>> Ok M53 - Set Ethernet IP ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the robot’s Ethernet IP address. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M53 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M53 A192 B168 C1 D100 ;set the robot IP to 192.168.1.100 >>> Ok M54 - Set Ethernet DNS ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet DNS address. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M54 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M54 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the DNS server to 192.168.1.1 >>> Ok M55 - Set Ethernet Gateway ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet gateway address. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M55 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M55 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the gateway to 192.168.1.1 >>> Ok M56 - Set Ethernet Subnet ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet subnet mask. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The mask is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M56 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M56 A255 B255 C255 D0 ;use the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet >>> Ok M57 - Get Robot IP ¶ Descriptions ¶ Get the robot’s configured IP address. Ethernet must be enabled with M50 A1 . Usage ¶ M57 Example ¶ M53 A192 B168 C1 D100 ;set the robot IP to 192.168.1.100 M50 A1 ;enable Ethernet M57 ;read the configured robot IP >>> IP:192.168.1.100 M58 - Get Ethernet Info ¶ Descriptions ¶ Get the Ethernet enable state, configured IP address, port, MAC address, DNS, gateway, and subnet mask. MAC bytes are reported in decimal. Usage ¶ M58 Example ¶ M51 B8844 ;set the TCP port M52 A2 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 ;set the MAC address in decimal M53 A192 B168 C1 D100 ;set the robot IP M54 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the DNS server M55 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the gateway M56 A255 B255 C255 D0 ;set the subnet mask M50 A1 ;enable Ethernet M58 ;read the Ethernet configuration >>> Ethernet:On;Ip:192.168.1.100;Port:8844;Mac:2-23-34-45-56-67;Dns:192.168.1.1;Gateway:192.168.1.1;Subnet:255.255.255.0 M60 - Set Axis W ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure the angle limits, home position, and servo pulse widths for axis W. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M60 [P<x>] [Q<y>] [H<z>] [A<t>] [B<u>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[x] Maximum angle in degrees. Q[y] Minimum angle in degrees. The limits must satisfy 0 <= Q < P <= 360 . H[z] Home angle in degrees, within Q <= H <= P . A[t] Minimum pulse width, integer from 36 to 1056 µs. B[u] Maximum pulse width, integer from 1892 to 2912 µs. Example ¶ M60 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;set W limits to 0-180 degrees, home 90, pulses 500-2500 us G90 ;use absolute positioning G01 W90 ;move W to 90 degrees, corresponding to a 1500 us pulse M61 - Set Axis U ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure the angle limits, home position, and servo pulse widths for axis U. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage ¶ M61 [P<x>] [Q<y>] [H<z>] [A<t>] [B<u>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[x] Maximum angle in degrees. Q[y] Minimum angle in degrees. The limits must satisfy 0 <= Q < P <= 360 . H[z] Home angle in degrees, within Q <= H <= P . A[t] Minimum pulse width, integer from 36 to 1056 µs. B[u] Maximum pulse width, integer from 1892 to 2912 µs. Example ¶ M61 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;set U limits to 0-180 degrees, home 90, pulses 500-2500 us G90 ;use absolute positioning G01 U90 ;move U to 90 degrees, corresponding to a 1500 us pulse M62 - Set Gripper ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure the gripper’s angle limits and home position. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. These angles define the range used by M03 S0 through M03 S100 when gripper mode is selected. Usage ¶ M62 [P<x>] [Q<y>] [H<z>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[x] Maximum angle in degrees. Q[y] Minimum angle in degrees. The limits must satisfy 0 <= Q < P <= 360 . H[z] Home angle in degrees, within Q <= H <= P . Example ¶ M62 P100 Q0 H50 ;set gripper limits to 0-100 degrees and home to 50 degrees M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move to 50% of the 0-100 degree range: 50 degrees G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper to 0 degrees M84 - Disable Steppers ¶ Descriptions ¶ Disable the stepper motors. The XYZ position reference is cleared; run G28 before the next XYZ move. Usage ¶ M84 Example M84 ;disable the stepper motors and clear the XYZ reference M85 - Enable Steppers ¶ Descriptions ¶ Enable the stepper motors. After M84 , run G28 to restore the XYZ position reference before moving. Usage ¶ M85 Example M85 ;enable the stepper motors G28 ;establish the XYZ reference before moving M203 - Set Jerk ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the jerk used for subsequent movements until changed. Usage ¶ M203 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] Required jerk in mm/s³, integer from 1 to 10000000. Example ¶ M203 S550000 ;set jerk to 550000 mm/s^3 M204 - Set Max Acceleration ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the acceleration used for subsequent movements until changed. Usage ¶ M204 A<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description A[value] Required acceleration in mm/s², integer from 1 to 50000. Example ¶ M204 A15000 ;set acceleration to 15000 mm/s^2 M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set both the start and end velocities for subsequent movements until changed. Usage ¶ M205 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] Required start/end velocity in mm/s, integer from 0 to 20000. Motion planning limits these velocities to max(F - 2, 0) . Example ¶ M205 S50 ;set both start and end velocities to 50 mm/s M206 - Set Axis Offset ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the working coordinate origin within the robot’s workspace. Subsequent absolute XYZ targets are relative to this origin. Use PositionOffset to read the current position in the working coordinates. Use M206 X0 Y0 Z0 to return to the base coordinate system. The working origin is not saved by M500 ; resetting or loading settings clears it. Usage ¶ M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[value] (mm) Working origin X coordinate in the base coordinate system. Y[value] (mm) Working origin Y coordinate in the base coordinate system. Z[value] (mm) Working origin Z coordinate in the base coordinate system. Example ¶ G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X20 Y-10 Z-360 ;move to the intended working origin M206 X20 Y-10 Z-360 ;make this point X0 Y0 Z0 in working coordinates G01 X20 Y0 Z0 ;move to base coordinates X40 Y-10 Z-360 G01 X0 Y0 Z0 ;return to the working origin M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;restore the base coordinate system M207 - Set Z Safe ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the lowest Z level that the robot cannot exceed. Usage ¶ M207 Z<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description Z[value] (mm) Z safe value. Example ¶ M207 Z-420 ;set the lowest permitted base Z coordinate to -420 mm M210 - Set Motion Parameters ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Cartesian motion parameters used for subsequent movements. Set these values once; they remain in effect until changed. Usage ¶ M210 [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[val] (mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] (mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] (mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Start and end velocities are limited to max(F - 2, 0) . Example ¶ M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s M220 - Read Parameters ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read robot parameters. Usage ¶ M220 [I<n>] Parameters ¶ I[n] : Parameter group; defaults to 0. n = 0 : read move parameters. n = 1 : read axis W parameters. n = 2 : read axis U parameters. n = 3 : read gripper parameters. Example ¶ M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;configure the motion settings used below M60 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;configure W M61 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;configure U M62 P100 Q0 H50 ;configure the gripper M220 I0 ;read motion settings >>> F:1500 A:15000 J:550000 S:50 E:50 M220 I1 ;read W settings >>> WP:180.00 WQ:0.00 WH:90.00 WA:500 WB:2500 M220 I2 ;read U settings >>> UP:180.00 UQ:0.00 UH:90.00 UA:500 UB:2500 M220 I3 ;read gripper settings >>> GP:100.00 GQ:0.00 GH:50.00 M360 - Select End Effector ¶ Descriptions ¶ Select vacuum, gripper, or pen mode for the robot’s end effector. Usage ¶ M360 E<value> Parameters ¶ E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen Example ¶ M360 E0 ;select vacuum mode M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;turn off the vacuum M360 E1 ;select gripper mode M03 S50 ;move to the middle of the configured gripper range G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper M360 E2 ;select pen mode M361 - Set minimum movement ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the minimum movement distance. The default and smallest allowed value are 0.1 mm. Usage ¶ M361 P<len> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Minimum movement distance, from 0.1 to 1000000 mm. Example ¶ M361 P0.1 ;set the minimum movement distance to 0.1 mm M500 - Save Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Save persistent settings to EEPROM, including motion parameters, axis/gripper calibration, robot geometry, and communication settings. The working origin set by M206 is not saved. Usage ¶ M500 Example ¶ M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set the motion parameters M500 ;save the current persistent settings to EEPROM >>> Ok M501 - Reset Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Reset settings to their defaults and save them to EEPROM. This also clears the working origin and XYZ position reference. Run G28 before the next XYZ move. Usage ¶ M501 Example ¶ M501 ;reset settings to defaults and save them to EEPROM G28 ;home again before XYZ movement M502 - Load Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Load saved settings from EEPROM. This also clears the working origin and XYZ position reference. Run G28 before the next XYZ move. docs.text: The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Run G28 before the first XYZ move after startup, disabling the motors, or resetting/loading settings. Commands that only set motion parameters or move W/U do not require XYZ homing. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>]
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Description X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (degrees) Axis W position, within the limits configured by M60 . U[angle] (degrees) Axis U position, within the limits configured by M61 . F[val] (mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] (mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] (mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Start and end velocities are limited to max(F - 2, 0) . The planner may reduce motion parameters to keep the XYZ step rates within their limits. When this happens, the robot reports Replace F<value> A<value> J<value> S<value> E<value> before Ok , with three decimal places. These are the effective settings for that move; the stored motion settings remain unchanged.

docs.text: G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to X0 Y0 Z-360 G01 X50 ;move to X50, keeping Y0 and Z-360 G01 W90 U45 ;rotate W to 90 degrees and U to 45 degrees G00 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;return to X0 Y0 Z-360 G01 W0 U0 ;return W and U to 0 degrees

docs.text: On Delta X 3, G2 moves counter-clockwise and G3 moves clockwise , viewed from +Z toward the XY plane. The arc starts at the current XY position and ends at the specified XY position, around the center defined by I and J. Z remains unchanged throughout the arc. Both I and J are required, including when either offset is zero. J specifies the arc center’s Y offset; the previously set jerk remains in use. Run G28 before XYZ motion. Endpoints follow G90 or G91 ; I/J are always offsets from the arc’s starting point.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>]
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Description I[offset] (mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] (mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] (degrees) Axis W position, within the limits configured by M60 . U[angle] (degrees) Axis U position, within the limits configured by M61 . F[val] (mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] (mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. These motion settings remain in effect for subsequent moves until changed.

docs.text: G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X50 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the arc's starting point G02 X0 Y50 I-50 J0 ;move 90 degrees counter-clockwise around X0 Y0 G03 X50 Y0 I0 J-50 ;move 90 degrees clockwise back to X50 Y0 Both arcs have a 50 mm radius and a path length of approximately 78.54 mm. Z stays at -360 mm.

M03, M04 - Output On / Set PWM / Vacuum On

docs.text: Turn on a Delta X 3 digital output, set a PWM output, or control the end effector selected by M360 .
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: M03 D<x> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y> M03 S<value>
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: M03 D[x] or M04 D[x] : Turn on a digital output. x = 0, 1, 2, 3 for the external digital outputs. x = 4 controls the selected end effector. With vacuum mode ( M360 E0 ), it turns the vacuum on. M03 P[x] W[y] : Set a PWM output. x = 0, 1. y = integer from 0 to 255; required. M04 P[x] W[y] : Set a PWM output with a larger value range. x = 0, 1. y = integer from 0 to 65535; required. M03 S[value] or M04 S[value] : Control the selected end effector, with an integer value from 0 to 100. Vacuum ( M360 E0 ): turns the vacuum on. Gripper ( M360 E1 ): positions the gripper within the range configured by M62 ; S0 is fully open and S100 is fully closed. Use separate commands for digital ( D ) and PWM ( P ) outputs. W is used only with PWM outputs.
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: M03 D0 ;turn on digital output D0 M05 D0 ;turn off digital output D0 M03 P0 W128 ;set P0 to 128/255, approximately 50.20% PWM M05 P0 ;turn off PWM output P0 M04 P1 W32768 ;set P1 to 32768/65535, approximately 50.00% PWM M05 P1 ;turn off PWM output P1 M360 E0 ;select the vacuum M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum G04 P500 ;keep the vacuum on for 0.5 seconds M05 ;turn off the vacuum M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move halfway between the configured gripper angle limits G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper

docs.text: I[n] : Parameter group; defaults to 0. n = 0 : read move parameters. n = 1 : read axis W parameters. n = 2 : read axis U parameters. n = 3 : read gripper parameters.
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;configure the motion settings used below M60 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;configure W M61 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;configure U M62 P100 Q0 H50 ;configure the gripper M220 I0 ;read motion settings >>> F:1500 A:15000 J:550000 S:50 E:50 M220 I1 ;read W settings >>> WP:180.00 WQ:0.00 WH:90.00 WA:500 WB:2500 M220 I2 ;read U settings >>> UP:180.00 UQ:0.00 UH:90.00 UA:500 UB:2500 M220 I3 ;read gripper settings >>> GP:100.00 GQ:0.00 GH:50.00

docs.text: Select vacuum, gripper, or pen mode for the robot’s end effector.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: M360 E<value>
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: M360 E0 ;select vacuum mode M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;turn off the vacuum M360 E1 ;select gripper mode M03 S50 ;move to the middle of the configured gripper range G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper M360 E2 ;select pen mode

docs.text: Set the minimum movement distance. The default and smallest allowed value are 0.1 mm.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: M361 P<len>
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Description P[len] (mm) Minimum movement distance, from 0.1 to 1000000 mm.
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: M361 P0.1 ;set the minimum movement distance to 0.1 mm

docs.text: Save persistent settings to EEPROM, including motion parameters, axis/gripper calibration, robot geometry, and communication settings. The working origin set by M206 is not saved.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set the motion parameters M500 ;save the current persistent settings to EEPROM >>> Ok
docs.title: Example

docs.text: Reset settings to their defaults and save them to EEPROM. This also clears the working origin and XYZ position reference. Run G28 before the next XYZ move.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: Load saved settings from EEPROM. This also clears the working origin and XYZ position reference. Run G28 before the next XYZ move.

docs.text: G-CODES FOR DELTA X S V4 ¶ G0, G1 - Linear Movement ¶ Descriptions ¶ The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage ¶ G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (unit) Axis 4 position. U[angle] (unit) Axis 5 position. V[angle] (unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] (mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. J[val] (mm/s3) Jerk of the motion. S[val] (mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] (mm/s) Finish velocity. For W/U/V, a unit is a degree for a rotary axis or a millimeter for a linear axis, according to its steps-per-unit configuration. Example ¶ G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 ; Set the feed rate to 1500 mm/s, acceleration to 15000 mm/s², jerk to 550000 mm/s³, start velocity to 100 mm/s, and end velocity to 100 mm/s. G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 ; Move to the absolute position (X0, Y0, Z-750). G01 X50 ; Move to X = 50 mm. G01 W90 ; Rotate to 90° on the 4-axis G2, G3 - Controlled Arc Movement ¶ Descriptions ¶ Add an arc move in the XY plane, keeping Z unchanged. I and J locate the center relative to the arc’s starting point. Use G90 absolute positioning for arc commands. In this XS V4 implementation, G2 moves counter-clockwise and G3 moves clockwise , viewed from positive Z toward the XY plane. Use the directions shown here when preparing commands for XS V4. Usage ¶ G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Use G03 for the opposite direction. Always include both I and J , even when one offset is zero. Here, J is the Y center offset; the previously configured jerk remains in use. Parameters ¶ Parameter Description I[offset] (mm) Required X offset from the starting point to the arc center. J[offset] (mm) Required Y offset from the starting point to the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] , U[angle] , V[angle] :(unit) Axis 4, 5, and 6 positions, using the configured units for each axis. F[val] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] (mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. S[val] (mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] (mm/s) Finish velocity. Example ¶ G28 ; Home all axes. G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G01 X50 Y20 Z-750 F200 ; Move to the arc start at (X50, Y20, Z-750). G02 X20 Y50 I-30 J0 F200 ; Counter-clockwise 90° arc around (X20, Y20), radius 30 mm. G03 X50 Y20 I0 J-30 F200 ; Clockwise 90° arc back to (X50, Y20). Both arcs keep Z at -750 mm. The X/Y endpoints are absolute positions; I/J are offsets from each arc’s starting point to the center at (X20, Y20). Keep the center’s X coordinate nonzero for this implementation. G4 - Dwell/Delay ¶ Descriptions ¶ Pause the robot for a period of time. Usage ¶ G4 P<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description P[value] delay in milliseconds. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X50 G6 - Theta angle control ¶ Descriptions ¶ Specify the target Theta 1, 2, and 3 angles instead of Cartesian endpoint coordinates. Axis 6 is selected with R in this command. Usage ¶ G6 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [W<pos>] [U<pos>] [R<pos>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. W[pos] (unit) Axis 4 position. U[pos] (unit) Axis 5 position. R[pos] (unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] (mm/s) Cartesian feed rate. A[val] (mm/s²) Cartesian acceleration. J[val] (mm/s³) Cartesian jerk. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity. W/U/R use the configured units for their axes: degrees for rotary axes or millimeters for linear axes. Omitted F/A/J/S/E values keep their current motion settings, which also apply to subsequent moves until changed. Example ¶ G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G6 X20 Y0 Z0 F200 ; Move to Theta 1 = 20°, Theta 2 = 0°, Theta 3 = 0° at 200 mm/s. G28 - Homing ¶ Descriptions ¶ Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage ¶ G28 G90 - Absolute Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage ¶ G90 G91 - Relative Movement Mode ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage ¶ G91 G93 - Get Current Position ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read the Cartesian position stored by the controller. The response is always sent through USB, including when the command arrives on another port. Usage ¶ G93 Feedback ¶ The response contains <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> in millimeters, with two decimal places. Auxiliary-axis positions are omitted. The reported Z includes the robot’s configured vertical reference offset. For example, with a 188.5 mm offset and no user coordinate offset, a G-code position of Z-750 is reported as Z-561.50. Use M100 for automatic position reports in the G-code coordinate frame. Example ¶ G93 ; Read the Cartesian position through USB. Example USB response at X0 Y0 Z-750, with a 188.5 mm vertical reference offset: 0.00,0.00,-561.50 M03, M04 - Set Digital Output / PWM ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set digital output states or PWM values. M03 uses 8-bit PWM values; M04 uses 16-bit PWM values. Both commands can set digital outputs with D . Usage ¶ M03 D<x> W<state> M04 D<x> W<state> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y> Parameters ¶ M03 D[x] W[state] , M04 D[x] W[state] : set digital outputs. x = 0, 1, 2, … 15. state = 1 : turn on; state = 0 : turn off. M03 P[x] W[y] : turn on PWM pins x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. y = [0, 255] M04 P[x] W[y] : turn on PWM pins but with larger pwm range. x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. y = [0, 65535]. Always include W , including for digital outputs. Several outputs can be selected on one line, such as M03 D0 D1 W1 . Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. G01 Z-700 M05 - Turn Off Digital Output / PWM ¶ Descriptions ¶ Turn off selected digital outputs or set selected PWM outputs to zero. Usage ¶ M05 D<x> M05 P<x> Parameters ¶ M05 D[x] : turn off digital output pin x = 0, 1, 2, … 15. M05 P[x] : turn off PWM output pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. Several outputs can be selected on one line. Specify at least one D or P output; a bare M05 does not select all outputs. Example ¶ G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. G01 Z-780 G04 P300 G01 Z-750 G01 X50 Y50 M05 D0 ; Turn off digital output D0. M07 - Read Input Signals. ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read selected digital input states or raw analog input values. Several channels can be selected on one line. Usage ¶ M07 I<x> M07 A<x> Parameters ¶ M07 I[x] : Read Digital Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. M07 A[x] : Read Analog Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. Feedback ¶ I[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = [0, 4095] Example ¶ M07 I0 I3 A2 ; Read digital inputs I0 and I3, and analog input A2. Example responses; values depend on the connected signals: I0 V1 I3 V0 A2 V3946 M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically. ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure automatic input reports. Digital inputs report state changes; analog inputs report sampled values at the requested interval. Usage ¶ M08 I<pin> [B<enable>] [P<port>] M08 A<pin> [C<period_us>] [P<port>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Values and function I<pin> Digital input index: 0 – 7 . Several inputs can be selected on one line. B<enable> Digital reports: 1 enables reporting; 0 disables it. Default: 1 when omitted. A<pin> Analog input index: 0 – 3 . Several channels can be selected on one line. C<period_us> Requested analog report interval in microseconds. Default: 500000 (500 ms) when omitted. The I/O board determines the supported minimum interval and the value used to disable analog reports. P<port> Report destination: 0 = USB, 1 = RS232, 3 = TTL, 4 = Ethernet (RJ45). The startup report destination is USB. Open the selected port before requesting reports on it. RS485 ( P2 ) is rejected with Unknown: This function cannot be used on RS485! . Feedback ¶ I[x] V[val] : return auto read digital input value x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : return auto read analog input value x = pin number val = [0, 4095] Example ¶ M08 I3 B1 P0 ; Report changes on input I3 through USB. M08 A2 C500000 P0 ; Request analog input A2 reports every 500 ms through USB. Example automatic reports; values depend on the connected signals: I3 V0 A2 V2478 To stop automatic reports for digital input I3: M08 I3 B0 M40 - Open RS232 port. ¶ Descriptions ¶ Enable/Disable RS232 port and set baudrate. Usage ¶ M40 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters ¶ M40 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close RS232 port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close port B[y] : baud rate. Example ¶ M40 A1 B115200 ;Open RS232 port and set baudrate at 115200 M41 - Open RS485 port ¶ Descriptions ¶ Enable/Disable RS485 port and set baudrate. Usage ¶ M41 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters ¶ M41 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close RS485 port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close Port B[y] : baud rate. Note: When control Delta X S via RS485, after each time sending a G-code command to the robot, you must wait for a response from the robot before sending the next G-code command. Otherwise, the communication will not be successful. Example ¶ M41 A1 B115200 ;Open RS485 port and set baudrate at 115200 M42 - Open TTL port. ¶ Descriptions ¶ Enable/Disable TTL port and set baudrate. Usage ¶ M42 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters ¶ M42 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close TTL port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close Port B[y] : baud rate. Example ¶ M42 A1 B115200 ;Open TTL port and set baudrate at 115200 M49 - Get Ports Config ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read the enabled state and configured baud rate of USB, RS232, RS485, and TTL, followed by the Ethernet enabled state and server port number. Usage ¶ M49 Example ¶ M49 Example response; values depend on the current configuration: USB:1 BAUD:115200 RS232:0 BAUD:115200 RS485:1 BAUD:115200 TTL:1 BAUD:115200 RJ45:1 Port:8080 Ok M50 - Enable RJ45 ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command can be used to enable or disable RJ45 port. Usage ¶ M50 A<x> Parameter ¶ A[x] x = 1 : enable RJ45 x = 0 : disable RJ45 Example ¶ M50 A1 ; enable RJ45 M51 - Set Ethernet Port ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set ethernet port number Usage ¶ M51 B<x> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description B[x] port number Example ¶ M51 B8080 ; set ethernet port M52 - Set MAC Device ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the robot’s MAC address and save it to EEPROM. Usage ¶ Provide all six bytes in A:B:C:D:E:F order, using decimal integers from 0 to 255. M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number E[u] number F[v] number Example ¶ M52 A2 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 ; Set MAC address 02:17:22:2D:38:43 (hex). Response: Ok M53 - Set Ethernet IP ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the robot’s Ethernet IP address for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four address octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage ¶ M53 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M53 A192 B168 C1 D5 ; Set the robot IP address to 192.168.1.5. Response: Ok M54 - Set Ethernet DNS ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet DNS server address for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four address octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage ¶ M54 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M54 A192 B168 C1 D1 ; Set the DNS server to 192.168.1.1. Response: Ok M55 - Set Ethernet Gateway ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet gateway address for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four address octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage ¶ M55 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ ; set ethernet gateway address 192.168.1.1 M55 A192 B168 C1 D1 M56 - Set Ethernet Subnet ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the Ethernet subnet mask for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four mask octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage ¶ M56 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter ¶ Parameter Description A[x] number B[y] number C[z] number D[t] number Example ¶ M56 A255 B255 C255 D0 ; Set the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0. M57 - Get Robot IP ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read the active Ethernet IP address and server port number. Enable Ethernet with M50 A1 and connect the Ethernet cable before sending this command. The response has the form IP:<address>:<port> . If Ethernet is unavailable, the response indicates that RJ45 is disabled, the Ethernet hardware is missing, or the cable is disconnected. Usage ¶ M57 Example ¶ M57 Example response with IP address 192.168.1.5 and server port 8080: IP:192.168.1.5:8080 M60 - Set Axis 4 Parameters ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure axis 4. Units are degrees for a rotary axis or millimeters for a linear axis, according to the steps-per-unit setting. Use M500 to store the configuration in EEPROM. Usage ¶ M60 [D<val>] [E<val>] [I<val>] [S<val>] [R<val>] [U<val>] [P<val>] [Q<val>] [H<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [F<val>] Parameter ¶ D[val] : enable axis 4 val = 1 : enable axis 4 val = 0 : disable axis 4 E[val] : enable endstop val = 1 : enable axis 4 endstop val = 0 : disable axis 4 endstop I[val] : set invert endstop logic level val = 1 : axis 4 endstop invert val = 0 : axis 4 endstop non-invert S[val] : (unit/s) homing speed R[val] : (unit) distance to back away from the endstop during homing U[val] : (step/unit) set step/unit parameter P[val] : (unit) set max position Q[val] : (unit) set min position H[val] : (unit) set home position A[val] : (unit/s²) maximum acceleration J[val] : (unit/s³) maximum jerk F[val] : (unit/s) maximum velocity Example ¶ M60 D1 E1 I0 S30 R20 U8.333330 P180 Q-179 H2 A150000 J5000000 F2000 M61 - Set Axis 5 Parameters ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure axis 5. Units are degrees for a rotary axis or millimeters for a linear axis, according to the steps-per-unit setting. Use M500 to store the configuration in EEPROM. Usage ¶ M61 [D<val>] [E<val>] [I<val>] [S<val>] [R<val>] [U<val>] [P<val>] [Q<val>] [H<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [F<val>] Parameter ¶ D[val] : enable axis 5 val = 1 : enable val = 0 : disable E[val] : enable endstop val = 1 : enable axis 5 endstop val = 0 : disable axis 5 endstop I[val] : set invert endstop logic level val = 1 : axis 5 endstop invert val = 0 : axis 5 endstop non-invert S[val] : (unit/s) homing speed R[val] : (unit) distance to back away from the endstop during homing U[val] : (step/unit) set step/unit parameter P[val] : (unit) set max position Q[val] : (unit) set min position H[val] : (unit) set home position A[val] : (unit/s²) maximum acceleration J[val] : (unit/s³) maximum jerk F[val] : (unit/s) maximum velocity Example ¶ M61 D1 E1 I0 S30 R20 U8.888888 P95 Q-100 H2 A20000 J2000000 F2000 M62 - Set Axis 6 Parameters ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure axis 6. Units are degrees for a rotary axis or millimeters for a linear axis, according to the steps-per-unit setting. Use M500 to store the configuration in EEPROM. Usage ¶ M62 [D<val>] [E<val>] [I<val>] [S<val>] [R<val>] [U<val>] [P<val>] [Q<val>] [H<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [F<val>] Parameter ¶ D[val] : enable axis 6 val = 1 : enable val = 0 : disable E[val] : enable endstop val = 1 : enable axis 6 endstop val = 0 : disable axis 6 endstop I[val] : set invert endstop logic level val = 1 : axis 6 endstop invert val = 0 : axis 6 endstop non-invert S[val] : (unit/s) homing speed R[val] : (unit) distance to back away from the endstop during homing U[val] : (step/unit) set step/unit parameter P[val] : (unit) set max position Q[val] : (unit) set min position H[val] : (unit) set home position A[val] : (unit/s²) maximum acceleration J[val] : (unit/s³) maximum jerk F[val] : (unit/s) maximum velocity Example ¶ M62 D1 E1 I0 S30 R20 U8.333333 P20 Q-100 H1 A15000 J500000 F4000 M84 - Disable Steppers ¶ Descriptions ¶ This command can be used to disable steppers. Usage ¶ M84 M100 - Set Auto Feedback Position ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure automatic position reports and their destination port. Usage ¶ M100 [A<mode>] [B<time>] [C<port>] Parameter ¶ A[mode] : reporting mode. 0 : disable reports. 1 : report periodically during movement. 2 : report periodically during movement and while idle. B[time] : report interval in milliseconds. Use at least 10 ; a value below 10 disables reporting. C[port] : destination port. 0 : USB. 1 : RS232. 3 : TTL. 4 : Ethernet (RJ45). RS485 ( C2 ) is rejected with Unknown: This function cannot be used on RS485! . Open the selected port before requesting reports on it. Each report starts with Position: , followed by X/Y/Z and the positions of enabled W/U/V axes in that order. Values have two decimal places. Example ¶ M100 A1 B200 C0 ; Report position on USB every 200 ms during movement. Example report with auxiliary axes disabled: Position:0.00,0.00,-750.00 To report every 200 ms even while idle: M100 A2 B200 C0 To stop automatic position reports: M100 A0 C0 M203 - Set Jerk ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement jerk of end effector. Usage ¶ M203 J<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description J[value] (mm/s³) required jerk value. Omitting J returns Unknown:Gcode wrong! . Example ¶ M203 J1200000 ;set jerk = 1.200.000 mm/s^3 M204 - Set Max Acceleration ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set movement acceleration. Usage ¶ M204 A<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description A[value] (mm/s²) required end-effector acceleration. Omitting A returns Unknown:Gcode wrong! . Example ¶ M204 A15000 ;set accel = 15000 mm/s^2 M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set both the start and end velocity of a movement segment to the same value. Usage ¶ M205 S<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description S[value] (mm/s) required start and end velocity. Omitting S returns Unknown:Gcode wrong! . Example ¶ M205 S40 ; Set both start and end velocity to 40 mm/s. M206 - Set Axis Offset ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the origin offset used by absolute movement commands. The specified origin must be within the robot’s configured workspace and axis limits. Usage ¶ M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] [W<value>] [U<value>] [V<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description X[value] (mm) X offset value. Y[value] (mm) Y offset value. Z[value] (mm) Z offset value. W[value] (unit) W offset value, in the configured axis units. U[value] (unit) U offset value, in the configured axis units. V[value] (unit) V offset value, in the configured axis units. Example ¶ M206 X20 Y-10 Z-750 W0 U0 ; Set the XYZ origin to (20, -10, -750) and W/U offsets to zero. M207 - Set Z Safe ¶ Descriptions ¶ Set the lowest permitted Z coordinate and save it to EEPROM. A value below the workspace limit is rejected. A value above the home Z coordinate disables the additional Z limit. Usage ¶ M207 Z<value> Parameters ¶ Parameter Description Z[value] (mm) lowest permitted Z coordinate. Always specify Z; sending M207 without it disables the limit. Example ¶ M207 Z-870 ; Set the lowest permitted Z coordinate to -870 mm. The example requires -870 mm to be within the configured workspace and at or below the home Z coordinate. M210 - Set Theta Movement Parameter ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure Cartesian movement speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity for the Theta group. Set these motion parameters once; they apply to subsequent moves for this group until changed. Omitted motion parameters keep their current values. Usage ¶ M210 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[value] (mm/s) speed. A[value] (mm/s²) acceleration. J[value] (mm/s³) jerk. S[value] (mm/s) start velocity. E[value] (mm/s) end velocity. Example ¶ M210 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;set all theta movement para M211 - Set Axis 4 Movement Parameter ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure axis 4 speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. Enable the axis with M60 first and keep the requested values within its configured limits. Set these motion parameters once; they apply to subsequent moves for this group until changed. Omitted motion parameters keep their current values. Usage ¶ M211 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[value] (unit/s) axis 4 speed. A[value] (unit/s^2) axis 4 accel. J[value] (unit/s^3) axis 4 jerk. S[value] (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] (unit/s) end velocity. Example ¶ M211 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;config axis 4 move para M212 - Set Axis 5 Movement Parameter ¶ Descriptions ¶ Configure axis 5 speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. Enable the axis with M61 first and keep the requested values within its configured limits. Set these motion parameters once; they apply to subsequent moves for this group until changed. Omitted motion parameters keep their current values. Usage ¶ M212 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[value] (unit/s) axis 5 speed. A[value] (unit/s^2) axis 5 accel. J[value] (unit/s^3) axis 5 jerk. S[value] (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] (unit/s) end velocity. Example ¶ M212 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;config axis 5 move para M213 - Set Axis 6 Movement Parameter ¶ Descriptions ¶ Axis 6 movement parameters: speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. Usage ¶ M213 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters ¶ Parameter Description F[value] (unit/s) speed. A[value] (unit/s^2) acceleration. J[value] (unit/s^3) jerk. S[value] (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] (unit/s) end velocity. Example ¶ M213 F2000 A4000 J500000 S30 E30 ; Set movement speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. M220 - Get Current Axis Parameter ¶ Descriptions ¶ Read the current movement parameters of one axis group. Omitting I selects the Theta group ( I0 ). Usage ¶ M220 [I<val>] Parameter ¶ I[val] : axis index val = 0 : get theta parameter val = 1 : get axis 4 parameter val = 2 : get axis 5 parameter val = 3 : get axis 6 parameter The Theta group uses response labels F, A, J, S, and E. Axis 4 uses WF, WA, WJ, WS, and WE; axes 5 and 6 use the corresponding U and V prefixes. The selected auxiliary axis must be enabled. Example ¶ M220 I1 ; Read axis 4 movement parameters. Example response for an enabled W axis configured with these values: WF:2000.00 WA:4000.00 WJ:800000.00 WS:30.00 WE:30.00 M500 - Save Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Save the current motion parameters and supported configuration settings to EEPROM. IP, DNS, gateway, and subnet values set by M53–M56 are session settings and are not stored by M500 on XS V4. Usage ¶ M500 Example ¶ M500 ;Save settings M501 - Reset Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Reset settings to the firmware defaults and immediately save them to EEPROM. This overwrites the previously saved settings; an additional M500 is unnecessary. Usage ¶ M501 Example ¶ M501 ; Reset settings to firmware defaults and save them to EEPROM. M502 - Load Settings ¶ Descriptions ¶ Reload the saved motion parameters and supported configuration settings from EEPROM. Usage ¶ M502 Example ¶ M502 ; Reload the settings saved in EEPROM. M600 - Enable Emergency Stop Button ¶ Descriptions ¶ Enable emergency-stop monitoring using the standard XS V4 E-stop inputs I8 and I9 , and save the selection to EEPROM. Usage ¶ M600 A8 B9 Example ¶ M600 A8 B9 ; Enable emergency-stop monitoring on the standard inputs I8 and I9. M601 - Disable Emergency Stop Button ¶ Descriptions ¶ Disable E_STOP button. Usage ¶ M601 Example ¶ M601 ;disable E_STOP button Contact Us ¶ Store: https://deltaxstore.com Website: https://www.deltaxrobot.com Email: deltaxrobot@gmail.com Phone: +84 38 875 2005
docs.title: Delta X S V4

docs.text: The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>]
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Description X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] (unit) Axis 4 position. U[angle] (unit) Axis 5 position. V[angle] (unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] (mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. J[val] (mm/s3) Jerk of the motion. S[val] (mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] (mm/s) Finish velocity. For W/U/V, a unit is a degree for a rotary axis or a millimeter for a linear axis, according to its steps-per-unit configuration.
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 ; Set the feed rate to 1500 mm/s, acceleration to 15000 mm/s², jerk to 550000 mm/s³, start velocity to 100 mm/s, and end velocity to 100 mm/s. G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 ; Move to the absolute position (X0, Y0, Z-750). G01 X50 ; Move to X = 50 mm. G01 W90 ; Rotate to 90° on the 4-axis
docs.title: Example

docs.text: Add an arc move in the XY plane, keeping Z unchanged. I and J locate the center relative to the arc’s starting point. Use G90 absolute positioning for arc commands. In this XS V4 implementation, G2 moves counter-clockwise and G3 moves clockwise , viewed from positive Z toward the XY plane. Use the directions shown here when preparing commands for XS V4.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Use G03 for the opposite direction. Always include both I and J , even when one offset is zero. Here, J is the Y center offset; the previously configured jerk remains in use.
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Description I[offset] (mm) Required X offset from the starting point to the arc center. J[offset] (mm) Required Y offset from the starting point to the arc center. X[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] , U[angle] , V[angle] :(unit) Axis 4, 5, and 6 positions, using the configured units for each axis. F[val] (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] (mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. S[val] (mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] (mm/s) Finish velocity.
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: G28 ; Home all axes. G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G01 X50 Y20 Z-750 F200 ; Move to the arc start at (X50, Y20, Z-750). G02 X20 Y50 I-30 J0 F200 ; Counter-clockwise 90° arc around (X20, Y20), radius 30 mm. G03 X50 Y20 I0 J-30 F200 ; Clockwise 90° arc back to (X50, Y20). Both arcs keep Z at -750 mm. The X/Y endpoints are absolute positions; I/J are offsets from each arc’s starting point to the center at (X20, Y20). Keep the center’s X coordinate nonzero for this implementation.

docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Description X[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] (degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. W[pos] (unit) Axis 4 position. U[pos] (unit) Axis 5 position. R[pos] (unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] (mm/s) Cartesian feed rate. A[val] (mm/s²) Cartesian acceleration. J[val] (mm/s³) Cartesian jerk. S[val] (mm/s) Start velocity. E[val] (mm/s) End velocity. W/U/R use the configured units for their axes: degrees for rotary axes or millimeters for linear axes. Omitted F/A/J/S/E values keep their current motion settings, which also apply to subsequent moves until changed.

docs.text: Read the Cartesian position stored by the controller. The response is always sent through USB, including when the command arrives on another port.

docs.text: The response contains <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> in millimeters, with two decimal places. Auxiliary-axis positions are omitted. The reported Z includes the robot’s configured vertical reference offset. For example, with a 188.5 mm offset and no user coordinate offset, a G-code position of Z-750 is reported as Z-561.50. Use M100 for automatic position reports in the G-code coordinate frame.

M03, M04 - Set Digital Output / PWM

docs.text: Set digital output states or PWM values. M03 uses 8-bit PWM values; M04 uses 16-bit PWM values. Both commands can set digital outputs with D .
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: M03 D<x> W<state> M04 D<x> W<state> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y>
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: M03 D[x] W[state] , M04 D[x] W[state] : set digital outputs. x = 0, 1, 2, … 15. state = 1 : turn on; state = 0 : turn off. M03 P[x] W[y] : turn on PWM pins x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. y = [0, 255] M04 P[x] W[y] : turn on PWM pins but with larger pwm range. x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. y = [0, 65535]. Always include W , including for digital outputs. Several outputs can be selected on one line, such as M03 D0 D1 W1 .
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. G01 Z-700
docs.title: Example

docs.text: Turn off selected digital outputs or set selected PWM outputs to zero.

docs.text: M05 D[x] : turn off digital output pin x = 0, 1, 2, … 15. M05 P[x] : turn off PWM output pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. Several outputs can be selected on one line. Specify at least one D or P output; a bare M05 does not select all outputs.
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. G01 Z-780 G04 P300 G01 Z-750 G01 X50 Y50 M05 D0 ; Turn off digital output D0.

docs.text: Configure automatic input reports. Digital inputs report state changes; analog inputs report sampled values at the requested interval.
docs.title: Descriptions

docs.text: M08 I<pin> [B<enable>] [P<port>] M08 A<pin> [C<period_us>] [P<port>]
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Parameter Values and function I<pin> Digital input index: 0 – 7 . Several inputs can be selected on one line. B<enable> Digital reports: 1 enables reporting; 0 disables it. Default: 1 when omitted. A<pin> Analog input index: 0 – 3 . Several channels can be selected on one line. C<period_us> Requested analog report interval in microseconds. Default: 500000 (500 ms) when omitted. The I/O board determines the supported minimum interval and the value used to disable analog reports. P<port> Report destination: 0 = USB, 1 = RS232, 3 = TTL, 4 = Ethernet (RJ45). The startup report destination is USB. Open the selected port before requesting reports on it. RS485 ( P2 ) is rejected with Unknown: This function cannot be used on RS485! .
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: I[x] V[val] : return auto read digital input value x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : return auto read analog input value x = pin number val = [0, 4095]
