If the physical emergency-stop button was pressed, release it only after the cause has been resolved. A serial Resume command does not release the physical button. Confirm that no unwanted commands are waiting to run. The examples in this guide send one movement at a time. If you previously sent several movements ahead, follow Clear pending commands before resuming. Send: Emergency:Resume XS replies Delta:Resume ; X3 uses its configured completion reply, normally Ok . Resume allows commands to run again; it does not confirm the robot’s position or home it. Check that the homing path is clear, then send: G28 Wait for homing to finish before sending the next command. Re-homing is especially necessary if the stop interrupted homing, the motors were disabled, or the mechanism was moved. Restore absolute positioning and check the position, sending each line separately: G90 Position Review the next target and motion settings, then send a new movement command when ready. Do not assume the interrupted move reached its original target.
docs.title: Recover after an emergency stop

docs.text: Emergency:Stop does not guarantee that queued commands have been cleared. Resume may allow pending commands to execute. On XS V5 , after the robot has stopped and before Resume, you can discard pending G-code commands with: Robot:QueueClear This clears waiting commands; it does not stop an active movement. It is not available in the X3 or XS V4 firmware covered here. For X3 or XS V4 , if you are unsure which commands remain queued, use the controller restart procedure below instead of resuming that queue.
docs.title: Clear pending commands

docs.text: To request a pause, send: Emergency:Pause The firmware replies Delta:Pause . Before sending Emergency:Resume , review the robot state and any pending commands as described above. Send a new target for the next movement; Resume does not complete the interrupted path automatically.
docs.title: Pause and resume

docs.text: When a controller restart is required, first stop movement and stop sending commands, then send: Emergency:Reset The firmware replies Delta:Reset and restarts. The USB connection may disconnect; wait for the controller to restart, then reconnect Termite if needed. Send IsDelta to check communication, run G28 after checking the homing path, and select G90 before using the absolute movement examples again. Re-enter any settings that were not saved before the restart.
docs.title: Restart the controller

docs.text: Let the current movement finish, then click Termite’s connection status field to close the COM port, or close Termite. You do not need Emergency:Stop just to disconnect after normal operation. Closing the terminal does not stop a movement already executing.
docs.title: 8. Disconnect normally

docs.text: Symptom What to check The robot does not appear in Device Manager Check power, the USB data cable, and the USB port. If Windows reports a driver issue, install the driver appropriate to the robot’s USB interface. Termite cannot open the COM port Select the correct port and close any other application using it. The sent command appears, but there is no robot reply Check that the port is connected, the baud rate is 115200 , and Append CR-LF is selected. Local echo is not a reply from the robot. The received text is unreadable Check the baud rate, data bits, parity, and stop bits against the settings above. IsDelta works but the robot will not move Check motor power and the stop state. If stopped, follow Emergency stop and recovery , then home with G28 and read any returned error. A movement command is rejected Check the command reference for the installed firmware, the current G90/G91 mode, and the robot’s workspace. For further commands, use the matching X3 reference , XS V4 reference , or XS V5 reference .
docs.title: Troubleshooting

docs.text: DeltaXStudio — Blockly Programming ¶ Use Programs to build a task by connecting blocks. A task can control robot movement, operate the end effector, process camera images, or combine detection with picking. Start here to learn the editor: create a program, connect its blocks, check and save it, then run a test. Connect the robot and check its tool using System Setup before testing movement. Camera-based examples list their own Calibration and Vision requirements. For built-in picking, follow Pick & Place . Start a program ¶ Open Programs and select the Blockly view. Click New for an empty workspace, or open Templates and choose a starting program. Save any changes you want to keep before replacing the current workspace. Template Starting point What to configure Stationary pick & place One pick followed by one place. Pick and place poses, working heights, and end effector. Conveyor pick & place A detection loop with an empty-result check and tracking configuration. Encoder direction, tracker selection, tooling, and pick/place inputs. Sort two object types Separate branches for class indices 0 and 1 . Class mapping, destinations, tooling, and tracking when objects move. Template vision frame A per-frame vision workspace. Image processing, the actual template folder, and detection settings. Templates are editable drafts. Loading one does not start the robot, and required inputs may be intentionally empty. Fill them for your installation before running. Click Use template beside the example you want. Save the completed program under your own task name. Build with blocks ¶ Drag a block from the toolbox into the workspace. Connect action blocks in the order they should execute, and fit value blocks into inputs such as positions, numbers, or conditions. Use loops for repeated work and conditions to decide whether an action should run. Toolbox group Use it for Robot Control → Movement Robot movement and pick/place actions. Robot Control → IO & Settings End-effector setup, I/O, and robot settings. Vision → Objects Retrieve detected objects and read their properties. Vision → Image Proc / Detection / Drawing Process camera images, detect objects, and draw the preview. Conveyor Control Conveyor operation and tracking setup. Loops / Logic Repetition, conditions, and comparisons. Math / Variables Calculations and values reused by later blocks. Connect the blocks that belong to the same sequence and fill their required inputs. Check the units shown on each block. End-effector delays in blocks use milliseconds, while the parameter panels use Dwell in seconds: 100 ms equals 0.1 s . An end effector, shown as EE , grips and releases the object. A Tracker follows a moving object using the configured conveyor/encoder. Fill an empty input ¶ To fill a height or another numeric input, open Math , drag the number block into its white socket until it snaps in, then click its number to enter a value. Click a dropdown to choose an existing end effector, tracker, or object type. Open Math and drag the number block marked 0 into the required numeric socket. For a fixed Obj Pos , open Vision → Objects and drag Object Pos from into the input. Fit number blocks into its X, Y, and Angle inputs. This block only groups three entered values; it does not require Vision AI. For a detected object, use Get Object Pos from the object variable instead. Z Move and Z Pick/Z Place remain separate height inputs. Movement X, Y, and Z values use millimetres in robot coordinates; Angle uses degrees. Measure these for the installed tool. Values in the screenshots illustrate one installation. To reuse a value, open Variables → Create variable and enter its name. The set … to block stores a value; the small variable block reads it later. For motion settings, set F, A, J, S, and E once before the repeated picking sequence; they continue to apply until changed. Input How to choose it EE Select the tool ID defined by Configure End Effectors, such as 0 , on both pick and place. Tracker Select the configured tracker for a moving pickup; use None for a fixed position. Obj Pos Fixed [X, Y, Angle] values, or Get Object Pos from a detected object. Z Move A measured transfer height that clears the carried object and fixtures. Z Pick / Z Place The measured tool height for gripping/releasing the object. Check and save ¶ Click Check program to check the draft before saving. Read the reported issues and use Locate block , when available, to find the block that needs attention. A passed check does not verify physical clearance or values calculated while the task runs. A passed static check verifies the program structure. Check motion values and physical clearance separately. Enter a task name and click Save . When editing a saved task, use Update . Wait for the saved confirmation and check that no unsaved changes remain. Selecting a task in Saved Tasks loads it for editing. An existing task shows Editing and Update. A new task uses the name field and Save. Run and stop a task ¶ Before the first run, check the target robot, tool operation, coordinates, and clearance. Keep Auto Start disabled while developing the program. For picking, begin with one object and conservative motion settings. Open Programs and find your saved task in Saved Tasks . Clicking its name opens the blocks for editing. Click its green triangular play button to prepare a run. In Select Target Robots , select the intended robot. For the first test, use one robot whose setup you have checked. Click Run Task and observe the result. While the task runs, its play button changes to a square Stop task button. Use that button to end the test before making changes. The trash button deletes the saved program. Use the green triangle beside your task name to open robot selection. Select the robot that should execute your program, then click Run Task when ready for the test. The robot name shown is an example. A robot already running another task is shown as busy. Do not start Main Task alongside a custom movement task for the same robot. The header Run button starts the task selected in Run Button Task ; it does not simply run whichever program is open in the editor. Use the physical emergency stop when immediate intervention is needed. After a normal test, stop the task, edit the blocks, check the program, and update the saved task before running again. Program examples ¶ Choose an example after learning the editor controls above. Start with Stationary pick & place for your first movement program. Continue with a camera-based example once the robot, tool, and fixed-position cycle work. Movement examples ¶ These programs move the robot. Set the poses, heights, and tool for your installation before running. Example Vision AI Position source and next skill Stationary pick & place Not required Enter fixed pick and place positions; test one cycle. Conveyor pick & place (AI) Enabled Retrieve AI detections and track pickup with the encoder. Color filtering + pick & place Disabled Detect objects by HSV and pick them in one combined task. Test the vision-only color example first. Sort two object types (AI) Enabled Branch on two trained AI classes and place them at separate destinations. Camera-based picking requires completed Calibration and a working Vision method. Conveyor pickup also requires encoder feedback. Vision-only examples ¶ These tasks process camera images and send detections to tracking. Keep movement tasks stopped while testing their previews. Example Vision AI What to test Color filtering Disabled HSV mask, object outlines, and tracking output. Color + Template Matching Disabled Color candidates refined against reference images. The Vision setup guides explain how to prepare and tune each method. These examples show the actual blocks and their connections. After detection works, choose the picking task for your application. Enable Vision AI for movement examples ¶ Use AI for the Conveyor and Sort examples. Their guides include the model selection, main enable switch, Save System step, and detection check: Set up Conveyor pick & place with AI . Set up AI for sorting two object types . Keep Vision AI disabled for the color pipelines. Fixed-position Stationary pick & place does not require AI. Find the Vision AI and Template Matching switches Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . The switch beside the heading enables AI; the separate Filter switch controls object-size filtering. Click Save System after changing the configuration. This screenshot shows AI Disabled. Enable it for AI movement examples; keep it Disabled for the color pipelines. Create a picking loop ¶ Configure the end effector before the loop. For moving objects, also configure tracking and verify the encoder direction and selected tracker. Set the pick, place, and transfer heights for the installed tool and object; see Pick & Place parameters . Inside the loop, use Get Object in Robot Area and store the result in a variable. Check that the result is not None before reading its properties. In that branch, use Get Object Pos to supply the detected pose to Move Pick , then use Move Place with the configured destination, end effector, and tracker. When no object is available, skip the movement branch. Include a short wait in the loop before requesting the next object. The conveyor template provides this structure so you can adapt the inputs rather than assemble it from scratch. For sorting, branch on the detected object type and provide a destination for each class to be handled. Verify the class indices against the final Vision output, particularly when Template Matching supplies the object type. Keep movement inside the object-found condition so an empty lookup skips the pick. Combine Vision and movement ¶ With Vision AI enabled and verified , a movement task retrieves the tracked objects directly. The conveyor and AI sorting examples use this arrangement. For color filtering, disable Vision AI and the System Template Matching switch, click Save System, and build the image-processing pipeline in Blockly using the matching guide: Color filtering Color + Template Matching Put the image pipeline inside Vision in main flow and keep the movement loop outside it. The final detections must reach Convert To Tracking Object and Push To Tracking Manager so that the movement loop can retrieve them. Test the vision-only task and inspect its preview before adding robot movement. Drawing boxes on an image alone does not make the objects available for picking. For the supported combinations of built-in and custom tasks, see Choose how to run the system . For a complete combined program, follow Color filtering + pick & place . It shows the image pipeline, tracking output, tool setup, and movement loop in one task, with Vision AI disabled. Use a saved task at startup ¶ Once the program works reliably in manual tests, select it under Auto Run Task . Follow Enable automatic startup to configure and verify startup behavior. Keep Run Button Task and Auto Run Task set to the tasks you intend to use. If the program does not work ¶ Symptom What to check Check program reports an error Read the message, locate the block if offered, and correct missing inputs or invalid values. A task is missing or old behavior runs Confirm Save/Update completed and that you started the intended saved task. Run Task is unavailable Select a configured, connected robot that is not busy with another task. The loop runs but never picks Check detection, object class, Robot Pick Area, and whether final detections reach the tracking manager. Reading an object pose fails Check for None before using Get Object Pos or other object properties. A runtime error points to a block Stop the test, use Locate block if available, inspect its inputs and current values, then check and update the task.

docs.text: DeltaXStudio — Calibration ¶ Choose the setup that matches your installation. Each guide includes its own preparation, settings, capture steps, and checks. Follow only the guide you need. Stationary objects ¶ Use this when the objects stay still inside both the camera view and robot reach. Static calibration ¶ Capture two reference points on a fixed board. The conveyor, if present, stays stopped. No encoder required No calibration camera Open guide → Moving objects on a conveyor ¶ All conveyor methods require encoder feedback connected to DeltaXStudio . First choose who controls the conveyor, then whether a calibration camera is installed. DeltaXStudio controls the conveyor ¶ Fully automatic ¶ The software controls belt movement and uses the calibration camera to align robot points. Encoder required Calibration camera Open guide → Manual robot points ¶ The software controls the belt. You align the tool and capture each robot point. Encoder required No calibration camera Open guide → Operator controls the conveyor externally ¶ With calibration camera ¶ You start and stop the belt when prompted. The camera handles robot-point alignment. Encoder required Calibration camera Open guide → With manual robot points ¶ You control the belt and align the tool to capture the reference points. Encoder required No calibration camera Open guide → The selected guide contains the working-height and crop instructions for that setup. There is no need to read the other methods. After calibration ¶ Check the completion message and camera crop, then continue to Vision . If calibration stops or fails, use the troubleshooting section at the end of your selected guide.

docs.text: DeltaXStudio — Daily Operation ¶ Use this guide for an application that has already passed its setup and picking tests. For a new installation or an untested application, start with Pick & Place setup . Open the configured system ¶ Power on the installation using its normal startup procedure and wait for the controller to start. Connect your computer or tablet to the robot’s network, then open http://<Local IP>:3000 using the robot’s current address and the port configured for your installation. If the address no longer works, check the current IP in your router or through the robot’s access point. See System Setup for connection troubleshooting. If Auto Start is enabled, the configured task may start without pressing Run. Keep the work area clear during power-up and check the displayed task state before issuing another start command. Disable Auto Start and save before returning to setup or editing the application. Check readiness ¶ Use Dashboard and the camera preview to confirm the setup still matches the application you tested: The intended robot and required devices are connected, with no unresolved stop or error state. The tool, object supply, and place destinations are ready, and the working area is clear. For camera-based applications, the image, lighting, and detection crop are correct. Test objects have the expected detection and class. For conveyor tracking, the encoder responds to belt movement in the expected direction. The intended model, parameters, and saved task are selected. Calibration and AI training are setup activities; do not repeat them solely because the controller was restarted. If equipment moved or the application changed, use When the application changes to find the checks to repeat. Use the indicators to check required devices. Green shows a connection; gray devices in this example are disconnected. Start the application ¶ Use the start control that belongs to your tested setup: Application How to start Built-in picking with AI Confirm the configured detection is working. Check that Run Button Task is Main Task, then use Dashboard Run. Built-in picking with a Blockly vision task Start the saved vision-only task and verify its preview, then start Main Task. Custom Blockly movement or combined vision/movement Use the saved task’s play button, select the intended robot, and click Run Task. Configured automatic startup Confirm the intended task is already running before starting anything manually. The header Run button executes Run Button Task . Opening a program in the editor does not select it for that button. Do not start Main Task alongside a custom movement task for the same robot. Observe the first objects through detection, pickup, transfer, and release before continuing normal operation. If the result differs from the tested setup, stop and check the cause before increasing speed or supply. Check Run Button Task before using the header Run control. Auto Run Task is the separate power-up selection. For a custom application, use the play button on its saved-task card. This stationary task name is an example. Stop and make adjustments ¶ Use the normal task Stop control to end a run. For a custom task, use its stop button in Saved Tasks . Stop an externally controlled conveyor using its own controls, and confirm the required equipment has stopped before intervening. Before changing parameters or blocks, stop the affected task. Save settings or update the program, wait for confirmation, and repeat a controlled test before returning to normal operation. See Blockly Programming for program updates. If immediate intervention is required, use the physical emergency stop. Clear the cause and verify the robot state before resuming operation. If using Termite for recovery, follow Emergency stop and recovery ; a resume command does not confirm the robot’s position or home it. Find the right troubleshooting guide ¶ Symptom Where to check The interface does not open Connection checks Objects are missing, duplicated, or assigned the wrong class Vision : open the method in use and its troubleshooting section Picks consistently miss or objects fail to grip/release Picking and release errors A saved task cannot run or reports a block error Blockly troubleshooting The wrong task starts after power-up Automatic startup settings Alignment changed after moving equipment Calibration , followed by detection and picking checks

docs.text: DeltaXStudio — Overview ¶ Choose a guide for the work you need to do. The four-step setup takes a new camera-based Pick & Place installation through its first successful pick. Blockly programming and daily operation have their own guides. Where to start ¶ Set up Pick & Place ¶ Connect the hardware, calibrate the camera and robot, configure detection, and test picking. Follow this path when commissioning a new camera-based application. Start with System Setup → Write a Blockly program ¶ Build a custom movement sequence or detection task. Connect and check the hardware first; add Calibration and Vision when your program uses camera-based picking. Open Blockly Programming → Operate an existing setup ¶ Open the interface, check the system, and run or stop the application that has already been tested. You do not need to repeat calibration or training every day. Open Daily Operation → The Pick & Place setup path ¶ Stage What you configure Ready to continue when… 1. System Setup Network access and installed hardware. The intended robot, camera, and any required conveyor/encoder respond correctly. 2. Calibration The relationship between camera, robot, and conveyor coordinates. Calibration completes successfully and the corrected image and crop are correct. 3. Vision AI or color detection, with optional Template Matching. Each object has a stable detection with the intended center, orientation, and class. 4. Pick & Place Working heights, destinations, motion settings, and the selected task. Low-speed tests reliably pick, transfer, and release objects at several positions. Each method guide leads back to the next setup stage. Blockly is available whenever you need it. Color filtering uses Blockly during Vision setup; custom picking logic uses it during Pick & Place setup. Built-in AI picking does not require learning Blockly first. docs.text: DeltaXStudio — Pick & Place ¶ Complete Calibration and verify Vision before running the robot automatically. Choose how the robot will move first: built-in Main Task or your own Blockly program. Then configure that task and test one object. Choose how to run the system ¶ Vision supplies tracked objects; the movement task decides how the robot picks and places them. Choose the movement method that fits your application. Built-in Main Task ¶ Use the supplied picking behavior. Set heights, object selections, and destinations in Settings → Parameters. Configure built-in picking → Blockly movement program ¶ Define the sequence, poses, heights, and tool actions in blocks. Start with a saved example and adapt it to your application. Choose a movement example → Use the row below that matches your detection method and movement choice: Detection Movement How to start AI, with or without Template Matching Built-in pick and place Enable and test the configured detection, select Main Task for Run Button Task, then click Run. AI, with or without Template Matching Movement blocks Enable the configured detection, then run the saved movement task for the intended robot. Color filtering, with or without a Match With Template block Built-in pick and place Disable Vision AI. Run the vision-only task and check detection, then start Main Task. Color filtering, with or without a Match With Template block Movement blocks Disable Vision AI. Save and run one program containing both parts; follow Color filtering + pick & place . The header Run button executes the task selected in Run Button Task . When starting a custom movement task from Saved Tasks, do not also start Main Task for the same robot. Create and run a movement program ¶ Use Blockly Getting started if you are new to the editor. Then choose the program that matches your task: Program Use it for Stationary pick & place One pick and place at entered fixed positions. Conveyor pick & place (AI) Picking AI-detected objects with encoder tracking. Color filtering + pick & place Detecting by HSV and running the picking loop in one task. Sort two object types (AI) Sending two AI classes to separate destinations. Follow the selected example for tool setup, position and height inputs, checking, saving, and running on the intended robot. Enter the movement values in its blocks. For camera-based picking, complete calibration and check the configured Robot Pick Area before testing. After the program passes its picking tests, continue with Daily Operation . The parameter and destination sections below describe the built-in Main Task. Configure the pick and place parameters ¶ For built-in Main Task , open Settings → Parameters . If there are multiple robots, select the robot whose parameters you want to edit. Setting What to enter Pick Parameters → Pick Z (mm) The tool height at which the object is picked, in robot coordinates. Pick Parameters → Dwell (s) The time allowed for the end effector to grip the object before lifting. Place Parameters → Place Z (mm) The tool height at which the object is released. Place Parameters → Dwell (s) The time allowed for release before moving away. Other Parameters → Travel Z (mm) The transfer height between pick and place, with clearance for the object, fixtures, and destination. Motion parameters Feedrate F in mm/s, acceleration A in mm/s², jerk J in mm/s³, and start/end speeds S/E in mm/s. Keep start/end speeds within the selected feedrate. Robot Pick Area The part of the tracked working area assigned to this robot. Pick Z, Place Z, and Travel Z are absolute robot-coordinate heights. Determine them for the installed tool and object; values from another robot or a sample program may not fit your machine. Check the end-effector type and output configuration in Settings → System . Save the parameter changes and wait for the saved confirmation before running. Set pickup height, grip dwell, and motion for the installed robot and tool. Use measured values rather than copying the screenshot. Travel Z is an absolute transfer height in robot coordinates. Conveyor Z records the measured belt surface. Configure the tracked picking region assigned to this robot and check it against the calibrated workspace. Assign object types to place destinations ¶ For built-in Main Task, start with the point-based place mode and configure Place candidates under Place Parameters. Match each Object index to the class order in Vision AI Objects: index 0 is the first class, index 1 the second. Enter the destination X , Y , and Angle for each class you want to place. Use + Object type to add another class. The plus button on a row adds another candidate destination for that same class. Each Object index has its own destination candidates. Add only indices used by your model and enter reachable positions for your installation. Under Pick Objects Index → Config , select the classes this robot should pick. Save and verify the class-to-destination mapping using one object from each selected class. Choose which trained classes may be picked. All objects includes every class; the names shown are examples. To skip a class, exclude it from the pick selection. In point-based placement, an object without a valid place candidate is also skipped. Preserve the other class indices when removing candidates; do not remove a class name from the Vision AI Objects list to skip it. An empty Pick Objects Index setting means all classes. Do not use an empty setting as a way to disable picking. Make the first pick ¶ Use this procedure for built-in Main Task . For a Blockly task, follow the run procedure in its selected example. Confirm that calibration is complete, the intended model or vision program is active, and the camera recognizes a test object correctly. Check the pick height, transfer clearance, destination, and end-effector operation. Open Settings → System → System Control . Set Run Button Task to Main Task and save. Return to Dashboard and click Run to start the built-in pick-and-place task. For a conveyor setup, start the conveyor at a low test speed and introduce one object. Observe the pick, transfer, and release. Stop the task before adjusting parameters. Repeat with each object class and several positions before increasing throughput. Use the normal task Stop control to end a test. If immediate intervention is required, use the physical emergency stop. Select Main Task for Run Button Task during the built-in picking test. Keep Auto Start Disabled while commissioning. Correct picking and release errors ¶ The tool consistently misses by the same amount ¶ Open Settings → Parameters → Pick Parameters → Robot Center Offset . Apply the correction in robot X/Y coordinates. For example, if the tool is consistently 5 mm too far in negative X and 3 mm too far in positive Y, the required correction is +5 mm in X and −3 mm in Y. Add this correction to the current offset, save, and test again. Use Object Center Offset when the desired grip point is displaced from the detected object center and that displacement should follow the object’s rotation. Leave it at zero when picking at the detected center. If the error changes with conveyor speed, object position, or rotation, check tracking, calibration, and orientation first. A fixed Robot Center Offset cannot correct all of those errors. The tool reaches the object but does not hold it ¶ Check Pick Z, tool contact, vacuum or gripper operation, and the configured output. If the tool needs more time to grip, increase Pick Parameters → Dwell (s) gradually. Keep the delay only as long as needed for reliable pickup. The object is still attached when the robot leaves ¶ Check the release output and tool operation. Increase Place Parameters → Dwell (s) if the object needs more time to release before the robot moves away. A detected object is not picked ¶ Check that its class is included in Pick Objects Index, it has a valid destination, it enters Robot Pick Area, and the selected task is running on the intended robot. For vision blocks, also check that detections reach Push To Tracking Manager . Enable automatic startup ¶ Enable automatic startup only after the selected task has passed manual tests with the installed hardware and workspace clear. Open Settings → System → System Control . Set Auto Run Task to Main Task or the saved program that should start after power-up. Enable Auto Start , then save and wait for confirmation. Enable Auto Start only after manual tests pass. Auto Run Task selects the startup program; Run Button Task controls the header button. Test a controlled restart with the work area clear. The controller attempts automatic startup approximately 15 seconds after its application starts, subject to its connection and run-state checks. Auto Run Task is separate from Run Button Task. Check both selections. A custom automatic-start task is dispatched to the configured robots, so verify the program is suitable for every target in a multi-robot installation. Turn Auto Start off and save before returning to setup or changing the application. Setup complete ¶ The setup is ready for routine operation when low-speed tests reliably pick, transfer, and release each selected object class at several positions. For conveyor applications, verify tracking as well. Continue with Daily Operation for normal startup, checks, and stopping. To customize the application, use Blockly Programming . This is optional when the built-in task meets your needs.

docs.text: Blockly example — Color filtering ¶ Vision-only example · HSV Color detection setup This vision-only program detects objects from an HSV mask and sends them to the tracking manager as object type 0 . It also draws the detected objects in the camera preview. It contains no robot movement blocks. Complete Calibration and prepare Color filtering before running. Keep robot movement stopped while adjusting detection. Prepare the vision task ¶ Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Set the main Vision AI switch to Disabled and also disable the System Template Matching switch. Click Save System and wait for confirmation. To locate the switches, open Find the Vision AI and Template Matching switches and expand the screenshot. Open Programs. Load Docs_ColorFiltering_Draft if it is already in Saved Tasks, or click New and build the sequence shown below. Add Vision → Image Proc → Vision in main flow and connect the image-processing blocks inside it. Use Variables → Create variable to add the names listed in the table below. Use a set block to store each result and the corresponding small variable block as the input to the following step. Keep the robot movement program stopped until you have tested this vision-only task and its preview. Block program ¶ Docs_ColorFiltering_Draft: color filtering inside Vision in main flow. Click the image to inspect the blocks. Place the image-processing sequence inside Vision in main flow . Use variables to pass each result to the next block: Variable in the image What it contains Used by _croppe_image The calibrated detection image, later replaced by the annotated preview. Filter HSV, Draw Rotated Objects To Image, Set Preview Image. hsv_image The binary mask produced by Filter HSV and updated by the two Denoise Image blocks. Find Contours. new_contours Contours that pass the size limits. Find Rotation Objects From Contours. new_objs Candidate objects with centers, sizes, and angles. Drawing and Convert To Tracking Object. tracking_objs Objects converted for the tracking manager. Push To Tracking Manager. The drawing block uses the original detection image and new_objs . Send tracking_objs to tracking, then use the annotated _croppe_image as the preview. Variable names can differ, but the connections must preserve this flow. Values shown in the image ¶ Block setting Screenshot value How to use it Lower HSV / upper HSV [0,0,26] / [179,255,255] Accepts the full hue and saturation ranges while rejecting very dark pixels. Narrow the bounds for the actual object color and background. Morphology Close / Open Kernel size 1 for both A 1 × 1 kernel does not meaningfully clean the mask. Increase only as needed while inspecting the mask; excessive filtering can merge or distort objects. Find Contours Min area 20 , max area 200 Despite the field names, the current implementation checks both dimensions of each contour’s rotated bounding rectangle, in pixels. Both dimensions must be between 20 and 200 for this example. Convert To Tracking Object Object Type 0 All accepted objects from this pipeline use type 0. Use this same index in pick selection and placement logic. Push To Tracking Manager Filter unchecked The supplied example leaves this option off. These are the values in this screenshot, not universal detection settings. The white-object HSV example in the Vision guide uses different bounds for a different detection target. Check the result ¶ Click Check program and correct any missing connections. Enter your own task name, such as My_ColorFiltering , click Save, and wait for confirmation. In Saved Tasks, click the green triangular play button beside your saved task, select the intended robot, and click Run Task. The run controls show these buttons. This task processes images and contains no movement actions. Open the camera preview on Dashboard by clicking the camera in the scene. Temporarily connect hsv_image to Set Preview Image so you can see which pixels pass the filter. Stop the task before editing; Check program, Update, and restart it after changing the preview connection. Objects should form separate filled regions against the background. Restore _croppe_image as the preview after tuning. Check for one stable outline per object and no false objects on an empty background. If an object disappears, inspect the mask and size limits; if one object becomes several, inspect gaps and noise in the mask. Once detection works, follow Color filtering + pick & place to combine this pipeline and a picking loop in one task. Keep Vision AI disabled. If you prefer built-in picking, use the vision-only task with Main Task instead. Choose the robot for this saved task before clicking Run Task. The robot name shown is an example.

docs.text: Blockly example — Color filtering + pick & place ¶ Movement example · HSV + encoder Color detection setup Detect objects by color, pick them from a moving conveyor, and place them at a fixed destination. This example combines the image-processing pipeline and the picking loop in one saved task . Keep Vision AI disabled ; no trained AI model is needed. Complete System Setup and the appropriate conveyor Calibration , including encoder tracking. First test the vision-only Color filtering example until each object has one stable detection and an empty belt produces none. Stop that test task before using the combined program. Prepare color detection ¶ Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Set both the main Vision AI switch and the System Template Matching switch to Disabled , then click Save System and wait for confirmation. Keep both switches Disabled for this color-only detection pipeline. The selected AI model is not used. Use the HSV bounds, contour limits, and camera setup that worked in your vision-only test. The combined program must use that same detection pipeline so it supplies the same objects to tracking. Block program ¶ Docs_ColorPickPlace_Draft, saved in DeltaXStudio with a fixed destination, working heights, EE 0, and pickup tracker 0. Click to enlarge. Open Programs . If Docs_ColorPickPlace_Draft is in Saved Tasks, click its name to edit it. Otherwise start from your tested color-filtering program and add the configuration blocks and picking loop shown above. Save your completed version under your own name. The program has two parts. Put the image-processing blocks inside Vision in main flow . Connect the tool configuration, tracking configuration, PlacePosition assignment, and movement loop after that wrapper, outside its image-processing body . Image processing ¶ The vision section detects objects and supplies them to tracking. The camera pipeline reads Get Detecting Image, applies Filter HSV and the two Denoise Image blocks, finds contours, and converts them to rotated objects. Use Draw Rotated Objects To Image and Set Preview Image to display the result. The color-filtering example explains each variable and connection. Pass new_objs through Convert To Tracking Object with Object Type 0 . Store the result in tracking_objs and connect that variable to Push To Tracking Manager . These two blocks make detections available to the picking loop; drawing outlines alone does not supply objects for pickup. The captured draft uses lower HSV [0,0,154] and upper HSV [179,124,255] , selecting bright pixels with low saturation. Its contour size limits are 20 – 200 pixels on both rotated bounding-box dimensions, and both morphology kernels are 1 . Use your tested settings rather than copying these values for a different object or background. See Verify color detection for detection adjustments. Tool, tracking, and initialization ¶ The movement setup follows the vision wrapper, outside its image-processing body. Configure End Effectors defines tool 0 : a vacuum tool on pin 0 , with 100 ms grip/release delays and zero X/Y offsets in the screenshot. Set the pin, delays, and offsets for your installed tool. Select that tool ID as EE on both Move Pick and Move Place. Configure Tracking Parameters defines tracker 0 with Use Main Encoder selected and direction angle 0° . Match the direction to your calibrated conveyor. With Use Main Encoder selected, the encoder supplies the conveyor movement; the displayed Speed value is not a command to run the conveyor. The next block assigns PlacePosition = [100, 100, 0] using Object Pos from. This defines the fixed placement X, Y, and Angle. Home the robot and set motion parameters before the first test. To include this preparation in the program, add Go Home and Set Motion Params from Robot Control → Movement before the repeat loop. Enter F, A, J, S, and E once; they continue to apply to later movements until changed. Picking loop ¶ Read objects supplied by the color pipeline, then pick and place when one is available. Inside repeat while true, set detected_object to Get Object in Robot Area . Select Object Type 0 to retrieve the objects produced by this pipeline. The screenshot shows None , which accepts any available type. The condition if detected_object means “an object was found.” Keep the pick and place actions inside this condition so an empty lookup skips movement. Input Value shown Move Pick → Obj Pos Get Object Pos from detected_object , as shown. Move Pick → EE / Tracker EE 0 , Tracker 0 for encoder-tracked pickup. Move Pick → Z Move / Z Pick -650 / -700 : transfer and pickup heights. Move Place → Obj Pos PlacePosition, assigned [100, 100, 0] before the loop. Move Place → EE / Tracker EE 0 to release the same tool; Tracker None for the fixed destination. Move Place → Z Move / Z Place -650 / -690 : transfer and release heights. Measure the heights and destination for your installation before replacing these values. Use number blocks from Math for height inputs. To define PlacePosition, create the variable under Variables, connect Vision → Objects → Object Pos from to its set block, and fill X, Y, and Angle. Connect a PlacePosition variable block to Move Place → Obj Pos. This position block does not enable or require AI. See Fill an empty input and Pick & Place parameters for the inputs and height meanings. After placement, the loop requests another object. If no object is available, it skips the movement branch and tries again. Save and test the combined task ¶ With the tested color settings copied and the movement values adapted to your installation, click Check program and resolve the reported issues. Save under your own name, such as My_ColorPickPlace , and wait for confirmation. Use Update when editing an existing task. Stop the vision-only color task and any other movement task for this robot. The combined task supplies its own detections and movement; run this task alone for the test. Keep Vision AI disabled and Auto Start off while developing it. Home the robot and confirm the motion settings first. In Saved Tasks, click the green triangular play button beside your combined task. Select the intended robot in Select Target Robots , then click Run Task when ready. The task can begin picking as soon as an object becomes available. Open the camera preview from Dashboard. At a low conveyor test speed, introduce one object and observe its detection, pickup, transfer, and release. Then test an empty belt: the loop should skip movement when no object is returned. The illustrated run controls show the task play button, robot selection, and stop behavior. Stop the task before editing detection or movement settings, then Check program, Update, and repeat the test. If outlines appear but the robot never picks, check Push To Tracking Manager, Object Type, the Robot Pick Area, and the selected tracker. If the pickup error changes with conveyor speed, recheck encoder tracking and calibration. Correct unstable or false detections in the vision-only test before resuming the combined movement task. Choose the robot for this saved task before clicking Run Task. The robot name shown is an example.

docs.text: Blockly example — Color + Template Matching ¶ Vision-only example · HSV + templates Color + template setup Start with the color-filtering example , then check its candidate objects against cropped reference images. This is useful when color alone also detects unwanted shapes. Prepare the template folder using Color + Template Matching . Leave Vision AI and the System Template Matching switch off for this Blockly workflow; the Match With Template block performs the matching. Prepare the example ¶ Complete and test the color-filtering program first so you can see the candidate objects before adding matching. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Set the main Vision AI switch and the separate Template Matching switch to Disabled , then click Save System . To locate the switches, open Find the Vision AI and Template Matching switches and expand the screenshot. Prepare a template folder containing cropped reference images for your objects. In Programs, build the color pipeline shown below and insert Match With Template between object extraction and drawing. Select your prepared folder on that block. If no reference folder is ready, follow Prepare the reference templates before testing matching. The screenshot selects default ; choose a folder containing the reference images prepared for your objects. Block program ¶ Docs_ColorTemplateMatching_Draft captured in DeltaXStudio. Select your prepared template folder and tune the filter values for your objects. Keep the image read, HSV filter, denoising, contour extraction, and Find Rotation Objects From Contours blocks from the color example. Insert Match With Template after candidate-object extraction. In this program, its output is assigned back to new_objs , replacing the candidate list with the matched list. Connection Value to use Match With Template objects input new_objs , the candidate objects from contours. Draw Rotated Objects To Image objects input new_objs , after the matching assignment. Convert To Tracking Object objects input new_objs , after the matching assignment. Push To Tracking Manager The converted matched objects. Set Preview Image The image annotated with matched objects. Both preview and tracking must use the matched list. Keep the matching assignment before drawing and conversion so candidates cannot bypass the template check. Configure the match ¶ Select the actual template folder in Match With Template, then set its threshold and scale. A higher threshold is stricter and may reject valid objects as well as unwanted ones. The block’s scale is a percentage: 25% corresponds to 0.25 in System settings. The screenshot selects folder default , threshold 0.65 , and scale 25% . Choose your own prepared template folder and tune these values against representative images. The HSV, contour, and denoising settings are inherited from the color-filtering example . The current block also shows interpolation Nearest , border value 255 , and heading edges All four . These are the defaults retained in this draft; check the matching preview and reported angle against your prepared templates. The templates should use the same camera, crop, lighting, and object height as the test images. Check the final center, size, and angle. This example sets Object Type to 0 in Convert To Tracking Object, so all objects sent to tracking use type 0 ; it demonstrates shape filtering, not sorting by template type. See Configure Match With Template for the settings. Compare candidates and matches ¶ Click Check program and correct missing connections, then save under a name such as My_ColorTemplateMatching . Click the saved task’s green triangular play button, select the intended robot, and click Run Task. Keep movement tasks stopped for this vision test. Use the illustrated run controls if needed. First confirm that the color mask and contour settings produce useful candidates. Then inspect the preview drawn from the updated new_objs . Test valid objects and similarly colored objects that should be rejected. Stop before changing a block or its values. After editing, Check program and Update the task, then run it again and compare the preview. If all candidates disappear after matching, check the folder contents, template crop, object scale, and threshold. Once the final detections are stable, use the task layout in Color filtering + pick & place , retaining Match With Template before Convert To Tracking Object. Test one object with the completed movement inputs. Choose the robot for this saved task before clicking Run Task. The robot name shown is an example.

docs.text: Blockly example — Conveyor pick & place ¶ Movement example · AI + encoder Choose a movement task Use Vision AI detections and encoder feedback to pick objects from a moving conveyor and place them at a fixed destination. The program shown is saved as Docs_ConveyorPickPlace_Draft in Programs. Complete the conveyor Calibration , configure AI detection , and start Vision AI before running this movement task. Vision AI supplies the tracked objects; the Blockly program handles pickup and placement. For HSV color detection and the picking loop in one task, use Color filtering + pick & place , which keeps Vision AI disabled. Start Vision AI first ¶ Keep the movement task stopped. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . In Vision AI Model, select the model trained for your objects and its matching type: DET, ORI, or SEG. If you have no uploaded model, follow Upload and enable the model first. Enter the trained class names in Objects, separated by commas and in the model’s class order. Click the switch beside the Vision AI Settings heading until it reads Enabled . Leave Template Matching disabled for this example. Click Save System at the top right and wait for confirmation. Return to Dashboard and click the camera in the scene to open its preview. Place one test object under the camera and check that it has one stable detection with the correct class. Confirm that the detected object reaches the configured Robot Pick Area. Then complete and run the movement program as described below. Vision AI continues supplying detections while this task picks them. Set Vision AI to Enabled and leave Template Matching Disabled, as shown. Use the model and classes for your application, then click Save System. The Filter switch below Conf / IOU does not enable AI. If the camera image appears but no object is detected, check the main switch, model/type, class names, and Confidence value using Verify detection before picking . This example uses the results from Vision AI and does not contain color-filtering or Vision in main flow blocks. See Choose how to run the system for starting detection and a custom movement task together. Block program ¶ Docs_ConveyorPickPlace_Draft as saved in DeltaXStudio. Coordinates and heights illustrate this installation; click to enlarge. Setup before the loop ¶ Prepare tool 0, tracker 0, and the fixed destination before entering the loop. Configure End Effectors defines vacuum tool 0 on pin 0 , with 100 ms grip and release delays and zero X/Y offsets. Configure these values for the installed tool. Configure Tracking Parameters defines tracker 0 with Use Main Encoder enabled and direction angle 0° . Verify the selected encoder and tracking direction during conveyor calibration. Before the loop, Object Pos from assigns the fixed destination to PlacePosition . The working heights are entered directly on Move Pick and Move Place. Value shown Purpose PlacePosition = [100, 100, 0] Fixed destination X, Y, and Angle. Z Move = -650 Transfer height on both moves. Z Pick = -700 Height at which the tool picks an object. Z Place = -690 Height at which the tool releases the object. Measure the working heights for your robot, tool, belt, and destination. See Pick & Place parameters for the role of each height. Home the robot and set motion parameters before the first test. To include this preparation in the program, add Go Home and Set Motion Params before the repeat loop. Set F, A, J, S, and E once; they continue to apply to later movements until changed. Retrieve, pick, and place ¶ The loop uses a tracked pickup and a fixed placement. Click to inspect its inputs. The repeat-while-true loop assigns the result of Get Object in Robot Area to detected_object . Object Type is None , so the lookup is not restricted to one class. The if detected_object condition runs the movement sequence only when an object is available. Get Object Pos from detected_object supplies its pose directly to Move Pick. The pick selects end effector 0 , tracker 0 , Z Move -650 , and Z Pick -700 . Move Place reads PlacePosition and places at X100 Y100 , angle 0° , using Z Move -650 and Z Place -690 . It selects EE 0 to release the same vacuum tool, and Tracker None for the fixed destination. The loop then requests another object; a no-object result skips the movement branch. Adapt the program ¶ To build your own version, start from Programs → Templates → Conveyor pick & place and complete its inputs using the structure above. Match the program to the installation: Drag number blocks from Math into empty height inputs. For a fixed destination using a Move Place block with Obj Pos, use Vision → Objects → Object Pos from and fill its X, Y, and Angle inputs with number blocks. Select the configured EE on both pick and place. See Fill an empty input for these basic editor actions. Setting Check before running Tracker The tracker selected for the pick corresponds to the configured conveyor and encoder. Encoder Counts respond in the expected direction when the conveyor moves. Detected object The camera recognizes the intended type and objects enter the robot’s configured pick area. Pick and transfer heights The installed tool reaches the object and clears the belt and fixtures during transfer. Place action The destination and its tracking selection match the actual placement setup. Check and save the adapted task. Add type-based branches when different AI classes need different destinations. Test tracking ¶ Click Check program and resolve any missing inputs. Enter your own task name, such as My_ConveyorPickPlace , and click Save. Use Update when editing an existing task, and wait for the saved confirmation. In Saved Tasks, click the green triangular play button beside that task. In Select Target Robots , select the intended robot only. With Vision AI already detecting correctly, click Run Task for the first movement test. Start the conveyor at a low test speed and introduce one object. Confirm pickup, transfer clearance, and release. The green play button opens this dialog. Select your robot, then click Run Task to start the movement program. While the task runs, its play button becomes a square Stop task button. Stop the task before correcting heights, positions, or tool settings, then Check program and Update again. The header Run button starts the task selected in Run Button Task; use the button beside your saved program for this test. Test an empty belt as well: no-object results must not cause movement or pose-reading errors. Repeat at different object positions before increasing supply. If the miss changes with conveyor speed, check tracking and encoder direction rather than compensating only with a fixed position offset.

docs.text: Blockly example — Sort two object types ¶ Movement example · AI sorting Choose a movement task Send detected type 0 to one destination and type 1 to another. The program shown is saved as Docs_SortTwoTypes_Draft and uses encoder tracking for pickup. To build your own version, start from Programs → Templates → Sort two object types and adapt the two movement branches to your application. This guide uses Vision AI to distinguish the objects. Complete Calibration and use an AI model trained for at least two classes before starting the movement program. Set up Vision AI ¶ Keep movement tasks stopped. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Select your trained model and its matching model type, DET, ORI, or SEG. If it is not uploaded yet, follow Upload and enable the model . docs.text: Blockly example — Stationary pick & place ¶ Movement example · Fixed positions Choose a movement task Pick one object from a known, fixed position and release it at a fixed destination. This example uses entered poses rather than camera detections; it does not need a vision pipeline or conveyor tracking. Vision AI is not required for this example. The robot uses the positions you enter in the blocks. Complete System Setup and check the installed gripping tool before building the program. The program shown is saved as Docs_StationaryPickPlace_Draft . It defines the pick and place positions in variables, then performs one pick and one place. To build your own version, start from Programs → Templates → Stationary pick & place and enter the values for your installation. Block program ¶ Docs_StationaryPickPlace_Draft with the entered poses and heights. These values illustrate one setup; measure them for your installation. Configure End Effectors defines vacuum tool 0 on pin 0 , with 100 ms grip and release delays and zero X/Y offsets. The next two blocks assign PickPosition and PlacePosition using Object Pos from. Move Pick reads PickPosition; Move Place reads PlacePosition. Both select EE 0 and Tracker None because the object and destination are fixed. Value shown Purpose PickPosition = [-70, 0, 0] Pickup X, Y, and Angle. PlacePosition = [70, 0, 0] Destination X, Y, and Angle. Z Move = -650 Transfer height on both moves. Z Pick = -700 Pickup height. Z Place = -680 Release height. Keep this first example as a single cycle. Adding a loop would repeat the pick even if no replacement object had been supplied. Fill the inputs ¶ Use Dashboard jogging to find the pickup and destination positions with your installed tool, and record the required X, Y, angle, and working heights. Adapt the example, or complete the empty inputs when starting from the template: In Configure End Effectors, choose the actual tool type and output pin. Set the grip/release delays and note the tool ID, such as 0 . Open Variables → Create variable and create PickPosition. Connect Object Pos from, found under Vision → Objects , to a set PickPosition to block. Fill its X, Y, and Angle inputs with number blocks from Math, and connect a PickPosition variable block to Move Pick → Obj Pos. Object Pos from only groups the entered coordinates; it does not turn on AI. Repeat with PlacePosition and connect that variable to Move Place → Obj Pos. Enter the measured destination and fill Z Move and Z Pick/Z Place with number blocks from Math. Select the configured EE on both movement blocks. Set both Tracker dropdowns to None because these positions are fixed. Home the robot and set motion parameters before the first test. To include this preparation in the program, connect Robot Control → Movement → Go Home and Set Motion Params before Move Pick. Enter F, A, J, S, and E once; they continue to apply to later movements until changed. Input What to enter Pick pose The known object position and required tool orientation. Place pose The destination position and release orientation. Pick and place heights Heights appropriate for the installed tool, object, and destination. Transfer height A height that clears the carried object and fixtures throughout the move. End effector and delays The actual tool configuration and enough time to grip/release; check the units shown on the blocks. Motion parameters Values already checked for this robot and application. Determine coordinates using the installed tool. For the meaning of working heights and dwell times, see Pick & Place parameters . Configure the block inputs explicitly rather than assuming that values in a different program have been copied. Run one cycle ¶ Click Check program and fill any missing inputs it reports. Enter a new task name, such as My_StationaryPickPlace , click Save, and wait for confirmation. Saving the program does not start it. Place one object at the specified pickup position. In Saved Tasks, click the green triangular play button beside your task, select the intended robot in Select Target Robots, and click Run Task. Observe pickup, clearance during transfer, and release. The sequence should perform one pick/place cycle and finish. See the illustrated run controls if this is your first saved task. Stop before correcting a pose or height. If the tool reaches the object but does not grip or release it, check tool operation and the corresponding delay before changing coordinates. Click the green triangle beside your saved stationary task to choose the target robot. Select the intended robot, then click Run Task when the workspace and first-cycle inputs have been checked.

docs.text: Calibration — Fully automatic ¶ Calibration · Fully automatic Change method Use this method when DeltaXStudio can control the conveyor and a calibration camera is installed . Required: robot + main camera + encoder + calibration camera . DeltaXStudio controls the belt. Screenshots may show an earlier interface; use the field names in the instructions. Configure this setup ¶ Stop running tasks and keep Auto Start disabled. Check the robot and main camera connections. Confirm the encoder counts increase with forward conveyor travel. In Hardware Settings, enable and select the calibration camera. Check the main camera, robot, encoder, and conveyor connections. In Calibration Settings , select Camera Fov outside robot area and enable Use Conveyor . Set X Offset to the conveyor centerline’s X offset from the robot origin, in millimeters. Use the sign of the robot’s X axis. This positions the automatic approach over the belt; it is separate from Robot Center Offset used to fine-tune picking. Check Conveyor Z, save, reset the system, and wait for the devices to reconnect. Select and enable the installed calibration camera. DeltaXStudio controls conveyor movement. Check the working height ¶ Open Settings → Parameters and select the intended robot if more than one is configured. With the conveyor stopped, use the Dashboard robot controls to approach the belt surface with the installed tool. Reduce the jog increment near the surface and avoid pressing the tool into the belt. Read the robot’s Z coordinate at the belt surface and enter it in Other Parameters → Conveyor Z (mm) . This is the field called Z Conveyor in the reference manual. Set Travel Z (mm) , called Z Move in the manual, to a height that clears the carried object, belt, fixtures, and destination throughout the transfer. Save the settings before calibration. Automatic calibration uses Conveyor Z to calculate approach positions, so check this value for each configured robot. Enter the measured conveyor-surface Z and a transfer Z with adequate clearance. The pictured values illustrate one installation. Read the current Z coordinate while positioning the installed tool. Three object heights above the belt can be used as an initial estimate for Travel Z. For example, a belt at Z = -740 mm and a 20 mm object gives -740 + 3 x 20 = -680 mm . Verify the actual clearance and robot reach; this estimate does not account for every tool or fixture. If a jog command is rejected, check the displayed status, homing state, and configured travel limits before continuing. Place the board and select the crop ¶ Stop the conveyor and place the supplied board flat under the main camera. Align it with the belt and leave enough travel for the capture sequence. Check that the whole board is visible, sharp, and well lit. Open Settings → Calibration and click Start . Follow any board-orientation guidance. Select two opposite corners of the detection area in the corrected image. Cover the useful conveyor area. Exclude blank image padding. Click Apply . The system is now ready to capture the reference points. Keep the board aligned with the belt. X Offset describes the conveyor centerline relative to the robot. Select the useful detection area, then click Apply. Let the conveyor carry the board between points. Do not lift, slide, or rotate it relative to the belt. Capture the reference points ¶ The system moves and stops the conveyor to capture the two main-camera reference positions and encoder readings. As the board advances into the calibration camera’s view, the system aligns the robot reference points automatically and repeats the sequence for additional configured robots. Monitor the current step until calibration reports completion, then click Done . Do not manually jog the robot or reposition the board during automatic alignment. If the sequence fails, use the reported cause to check board visibility, available travel, camera-to-robot spacing, and approach positions before retrying. Confirm calibration ¶ Wait for successful completion; the system validates and saves the reference points. Click Done , then check the corrected image and crop. Wait for successful completion before clicking Done. Continue to Vision to verify detection before the first pick. During the first low-speed picking test, check several object positions and conveyor tracking. Repeat calibration after moving the camera, robot, or conveyor relative to one another. If this calibration cannot finish ¶ Symptom What to check Board not detected Focus, lighting, board orientation, and complete board visibility. Crop rejected Select a non-empty area inside the valid corrected image. Missing or reversed encoder feedback Check the connection and counting direction. Encoder feedback is required for this method. Board passes the capture area Check available travel and camera-to-robot spacing. Incorrect automatic approach Check the selected robot, Conveyor Z, and X Offset. Browser reconnects Wait for the current session state to reload before continuing. Use Stop or Cancel to end the workflow and wait for stopping to finish. Calibration Stop waits for robot motion already in progress; use the physical emergency stop if immediate intervention is needed.

docs.text: Open Settings → Parameters and select the intended robot if more than one is configured. With the conveyor stopped, use the Dashboard robot controls to approach the belt surface with the installed tool. Reduce the jog increment near the surface and avoid pressing the tool into the belt. Read the robot’s Z coordinate at the belt surface and enter it in Other Parameters → Conveyor Z (mm) . This is the field called Z Conveyor in the reference manual. Set Travel Z (mm) , called Z Move in the manual, to a height that clears the carried object, belt, fixtures, and destination throughout the transfer. Save the settings before calibration. Automatic calibration uses Conveyor Z to calculate approach positions, so check this value for each configured robot. Enter the measured conveyor-surface Z and a transfer Z with adequate clearance. The pictured values illustrate one installation. Read the current Z coordinate while positioning the installed tool. Three object heights above the belt can be used as an initial estimate for Travel Z. For example, a belt at Z = -740 mm and a 20 mm object gives -740 + 3 x 20 = -680 mm . Verify the actual clearance and robot reach; this estimate does not account for every tool or fixture. If a jog command is rejected, check the displayed status, homing state, and configured travel limits before continuing.
docs.title: Check the working height

docs.text: Stop the conveyor and place the supplied board flat under the main camera. Align it with the belt and leave enough travel for the capture sequence. Check that the whole board is visible, sharp, and well lit. Open Settings → Calibration and click Start . Follow any board-orientation guidance. Select two opposite corners of the detection area in the corrected image. Cover the useful conveyor area. Exclude blank image padding. Click Apply . The system is now ready to capture the reference points. Keep the board aligned with the belt. X Offset describes the conveyor centerline relative to the robot. Select the useful detection area, then click Apply. Let the conveyor carry the board between points. Do not lift, slide, or rotate it relative to the belt.

docs.text: Wait while the system captures the camera reference positions and advances to Find Robot Point 1 . Follow the prompt to bring the board center into the robot’s reachable area using the Dashboard conveyor controls. Use small position increments near the desired location. Stop the conveyor. Jog the robot so the center of its tool is directly above the board center. Align X and Y accurately while keeping the tool clear of the board; it does not need to touch the board. Wait until the robot and conveyor are stationary, then click Get Point . Follow the next conveyor movement prompt. At Find Robot Point 2 , align the tool over the board center at its new belt position, wait for motion to finish, and click Get Point again. Repeat for any remaining robots, then wait for completion and click Done . Align the tool center with the board center. Keep the tool clear of the board while aligning. The two points use the same board center at different encoder positions. Move it with the conveyor rather than moving the board by hand.

docs.text: Vision — AI + Template Matching ¶ Vision · AI + Template Matching Change method Use AI to find candidate objects, then compare them with reference templates to refine detections and reject unwanted shapes. Start with a working AI detector. Image capture, labeling, training, model upload, and activation use the shared AI guide . Need a model? Follow Capture, label, and train . Already have an RKNN file? Upload and enable it , then verify AI detection . AI detection already works? Continue with the template steps below. Keep movement tasks stopped while configuring and checking detection. Prepare the reference templates ¶ Capture templates with the same camera, detection crop, lighting, and object height used during operation. In DeltaXStudio, open Vision and select Template Matching mode. Create or select a template folder. In Images , select Cropped , open the live camera, place a representative object, and click Save Current Image . Choose or create a reference-image folder in Template Matching mode. The pictured folder name is an example. Open Crop and select the saved image. Draw a tight rectangle containing the complete object, with minimal surrounding background. Click Crop & Save . This replaces that saved image with the cropped template; keep training images in their separate AI project. Repeat for the required reference objects. Inspect the folder contents and remove unsuitable captures before using it. Save/apply the configuration and restart the relevant vision task after changing templates. Reset the system if it is still using a previously loaded template set. Check the resulting object index whenever templates supply the type. Template indices follow the loaded filename order, starting at 0 ; they are not automatically matched to AI class names. Keep a clear mapping from each index to its pick filter and place destination, and recheck it after adding or renaming templates. An empty template folder cannot validate candidates. Confirm the saved cropped images are present before testing this workflow. Example cropped template: keep the full outline and minimize surrounding background. Enable template refinement ¶ Use AI to find candidate objects, then match reference images around those candidates. Template Matching can update the center, size, angle, or type and reject candidates without an acceptable match. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Keep Vision AI enabled, then enable Template Matching . Select the folder under Templates . Click Open to check its images. Adjust Threshold , Scale , and Find options for the result you need. Save and apply the settings, then inspect the final detections in Dashboard. Compare object center, angle, and class with AI-only results. For AI + Template Matching, enable both switches. Select your reference-template folder and refinement options, then click Save System. The values shown are examples. Setting Effect Threshold Minimum accepted template-match score. A stricter value can reject incorrect matches but can also remove valid candidates. Scale Image reduction used during matching. For example, 0.25 means matching at one-quarter image dimensions. Good objects are rejected Template crop and lighting; reduce the threshold gradually while checking unwanted matches. Incorrect center or angle Template alignment, AI candidate orientation, and the enabled Center/Angle options.
