docs.text: Vision — AI ¶ Vision · AI Change method Capture images in DeltaXStudio → label and train in DeltaXHub → upload RKNN → verify detection. Before starting: complete Calibration , check the live camera and lighting, and keep robot movement stopped. Already have an RKNN model? Go to Upload and enable the model , then verify detection. Need to train a model? Start with Capture and download images below. Labeling and training require a DeltaXHub account and Internet access. From camera images to a working model ¶ Use DeltaXStudio for image capture and robot-side detection. Use AI Hub on deltaxhub.com for labeling and training. Stage What you should have before continuing Capture and download DeltaXStudio A downloaded project ZIP, extracted to an images folder on your computer. Upload and label AI Hub Images uploaded, classes defined, and every target object labeled and reviewed. Train AI Hub A completed training run for that server project. Download the model AI Hub The trained .rknn file and its class names in model order. Upload and activate DeltaXStudio The uploaded model selected, matching model type and classes entered, and settings saved. Keep the robot’s DeltaXStudio address available. Your computer needs Internet access for DeltaXHub and a connection to the robot’s network when you return to upload the model. See System Setup if the robot is still only accessible through its hotspot. Capture and download images in DeltaXStudio ¶ Create an image project ¶ Open the robot’s DeltaXStudio interface and select Vision in the sidebar. Set Mode to Vision AI . Beside the Project selector, click + New . Enter a descriptive name, such as sorting-parts , then click the check mark or press Enter. Confirm that the new name is selected. To add images to an existing collection, select that project instead. Open the Images tab. These images are stored on the robot controller; download them to your computer before uploading them to AI Hub. Click + New, enter a project name, and confirm with the check mark. This example enters sorting-parts. Capture representative images ¶ In the right-hand Camera Controls panel, check that the camera is connected. Set Image Type to Cropped , then click Open Live Camera . Check that the preview shows the calibrated detection area used during operation. Place objects in the detection area and click Save Current Image . Confirm that a new image appears in the list. Change the objects’ positions, rotations, and spacing before capturing the next frame. Include every class and the lighting, backgrounds, and object arrangements expected during operation. Select Cropped and open the live camera, then use Save Current Image to collect each frame. The object shown is an example. Review the saved images. Remove blurred captures, accidental duplicates, and unusable frames; check that one class or one pose does not dominate the dataset. Around 100 varied images can be a starting collection, rather than a fixed requirement. Keep some fresh captures for testing the finished model. Optional: capture a series with Auto Save With the live camera open, set Max images to the number of frames to collect and Min time (s) to the interval between saves. Enable Enable Auto Save while changing the scene between captures. Set the capture limits before enabling Auto Save. Leave automatic AIX annotation off for the first dataset. Leave Auto annotation with AIX off when preparing the first dataset. This guide labels the images in AI Hub. Turn Auto Save off when finished and review the collection before downloading it. Download and extract the images ¶ Close the live camera when capture is complete. Check the selected project, then click the download icon beside it, labeled Download project . Save the downloaded ZIP to your computer. Download the selected project with the icon immediately before + New, then extract its ZIP on your computer. In Windows, right-click the ZIP and choose Extract All . Open the extracted folder, then its images folder, and check that your captured images are present and readable. In the AI Hub steps below, upload the image files inside this folder . The project ZIP may also contain a labels folder; the image-upload button expects the images, not the ZIP or that labels folder. Create a server project in DeltaXHub ¶ Open deltaxhub.com and sign in. Select AI Hub → Projects → Create Project . Enter a descriptive project name and select Storage: Server . Server storage is required for the training workflow below. Local storage is for labeling and exporting data to train elsewhere. Choose the project’s label type using the table below. Leave Public off unless you intend to share the project. Click Create , then Open on the new project card. This is a separate project in DeltaXHub. Using the same name as the DeltaXStudio image project makes it easier to identify, but the images are transferred by the upload below. Open AI Hub and create a project. Select Server storage and the label type required by your application. DeltaXHub label type Meaning DeltaXStudio model type RECT A rectangular bounding box for locating an object without orientation. Suitable for simple position-based picking, such as round fruit. DET ORI An oriented bounding box for an object whose rotation matters. Label its direction consistently. ORI SEG A polygon or mask describing the object boundary, useful when the outline is important. SEG The project label type describes the annotation format. Classes describe the object categories, such as class_A and class_B ; create one class for each category the robot must distinguish. Open the newly created project to upload images and add labels. Upload images and create classes ¶ In the open AI Hub project, click the plus button in the left Images panel. Browse to the extracted images folder, select the captured image files, then click Open . Wait for the upload to finish and confirm the images appear in the list. Select one to check that the correct camera images were uploaded. In the right Classes panel, click plus to add the classes you need. Give them clear, consistent names. Check the class list and order before labeling. Keep a record of that order for the Objects setting on the robot. Upload captured images on the left and define object classes on the right. Label and review every image ¶ With an image and its intended class selected, draw a rectangle, oriented box, or segmentation outline around each target object according to the project’s label type. Check the Objects list. Correct the class of any mislabeled object and remove unwanted annotations. SAM can assist with every project label type: RECT, ORI, or SEG . It starts disabled. After selecting an image, enable SAM near the top of the editor and wait for it to become ready. First use on a new computer may take longer while the required files download. SAM needs a supported, sufficiently capable GPU; if it is unavailable, continue labeling manually. Review and correct every assisted annotation, including its box or outline, orientation where applicable, and assigned class. SAM assistance does not replace this review. Repeat for the remaining images. Review all visible target objects, including rotated or difficult examples, before starting training. Confirm the annotations are retained when you revisit an image, then click Back to leave the editor. Annotation in progress: review each outline and class, then label the remaining target objects. For ORI, keep the object’s reference direction consistent across images. For SEG, follow the actual boundary instead of including large areas of background. Assisted labeling still needs review; a plausible-looking outline can belong to the wrong class or miss part of the object. Configure and start training ¶ Find your server project in AI Hub’s Workspace tab and check its image and class counts. Click Train , or Retrain for a project with previous training runs. In the training dialog, select AIX New . Review Auto Configuration, or open Customize Settings to adjust the parameters. Review the displayed cost information and available credits, then click Start Training . Wait for the queued job to run and reach Completed . A queued job has not yet finished training. Start training from the project's Workspace card. Review the dataset, training configuration, and current cost information. Optional: custom training parameters Parameter What it controls Epochs The maximum number of passes through the training dataset. More epochs take longer and do not automatically improve results. The supplied example uses 100. Batch Size Images processed together in each training step. Choose a value that fits the dataset and training server memory; a larger batch is not inherently more accurate. Image Size Input resolution for training. The example uses 640 px. Higher resolution can retain small details but requires more resources. Learning Rate The size of the model’s update steps. Start with the offered default unless you have a reason to change it. Early Stopping Patience The number of epochs without sufficient improvement before training stops early. Example custom settings. Training time and credit estimates depend on the selected job. Improve dataset coverage and annotation quality before simply increasing epochs or image count. Inspect performance on fresh images as well as the reported training results. Review results and download RKNN ¶ Open the project’s training details and select the completed run in Training History . Inspect the training curves, class results, and confusion matrix. Check both missed objects and false detections; a high summary score alone does not verify the robot’s working conditions. Scroll to the downloads for that completed run. Click RKNN (best.rknn) and save the .rknn file on your computer. Keep it with the project name, label type, class names in model order, and training run. You will need this file and class order in DeltaXStudio. Select a completed run to inspect its results. Download the RKNN model for upload to DeltaXStudio. The Model (best.pt) download is a different format. For DeltaXStudio’s New RKNN Model upload, use the .rknn file. Upload and enable the model in DeltaXStudio ¶ Reconnect your computer to the robot’s network and open DeltaXStudio at its current IP address and web port, normally http://<robot-ip>:3000 . Keep movement tasks stopped while uploading and checking the model. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . At New RKNN Model , click Choose File , select the downloaded .rknn file, and click Upload . Wait for the upload-success message. Select the uploaded model in Vision AI Model . Select its matching type in the adjacent dropdown: RECT → DET , ORI → ORI , or SEG → SEG . In Objects , enter all class names in the trained model’s order, separated by commas. For example, enter class_A,class_B for a model whose classes are class_A at index 0 and class_B at index 1. Do not add a trailing comma. Set the switch beside the Vision AI Settings heading to Enabled . For AI-only operation, leave Template Matching disabled. Click Save System at the top right and wait for confirmation. Uploading the file alone does not select or activate it. Return to Dashboard , open the camera view, and place a test object in the detection area. Check its class, center, and orientation before starting a movement task. If the new configuration has not taken effect after saving, use System Control → Reset , wait for reconnection, and check again. Vision AI is Enabled and Template Matching is Disabled. Select your model, type, and classes, then click Save System. The pictured model and good,bad class names are examples. Class index 0 corresponds to the first Objects entry, index 1 to the second, and so on. Keep every model class in this list even when a class should not be picked. Configure that selection under Pick Objects Index . Conf and IOU use values from 0 to 1 . Start with the provided IOU default. Increasing Conf removes lower-confidence predictions, which can also remove valid objects; it does not improve the model itself. Change one setting at a time and inspect the live result. Verify detection before picking ¶ Keep movement tasks stopped while checking the camera preview: Each class is detected at the positions, rotations, spacing, and partial occlusion expected during operation. Each object has one stable detection with the correct center, orientation, and class index. The empty background produces no false detections. Once detection is reliable, continue to Pick & Place and start with one object at a low test speed. To refine AI detections with reference images, continue with AI + Template Matching before testing picking. If detection does not work ¶ Problem What to check Save Current Image is unavailable Camera connection, Open Live Camera, and a live frame in the preview. Captures are missing from the download Selected DeltaXStudio project and the extracted ZIP’s images folder. Project is missing from training Server storage, completed image uploads, and the correct project in AI Hub Workspace. Wrong model file selected Download RKNN from the completed run and upload the .rknn file. Uploaded model is not active Vision AI Model selection, matching type, main enable switch, and Save System confirmation. No AI detections Model upload, enabled state, model type, camera crop, and Conf threshold. Swapped classes Trained class order and the Objects list. Training results look good but real objects fail Fresh operating images, lighting, and annotation quality.

docs.text: Vision — Color filtering + Template Matching ¶ Vision · Color filtering + Template Matching Change method Separate objects by color → find contours → match reference templates → send the final objects to tracking. No AI training is required. Before starting: complete Calibration , check the live camera and lighting, and keep robot movement stopped. The object color must be distinguishable from the background. New to the editor? See Blockly for creating, checking, saving, and running a task. The pipeline for this detection method is described below. Prepare the color-detection task ¶ Disable Vision AI and the System Template Matching switch. Save and apply the settings. Stop any previous vision task before running its replacement. Keep both system switches Disabled. This workflow performs detection in Blockly. Open Programs and create a Blockly task with Vision in main flow . Prepare the reference templates ¶ Capture templates with the same camera, detection crop, lighting, and object height used during operation. In DeltaXStudio, open Vision and select Template Matching mode. Create or select a template folder. In Images , select Cropped , open the live camera, place a representative object, and click Save Current Image . Capture a representative object into your template folder using Cropped camera images. Open Crop and select the saved image. Draw a tight rectangle containing the complete object, with minimal surrounding background. Click Crop & Save . This replaces that saved image with the cropped template. Use separate captures if you also need to keep the full frames. Repeat for the required reference objects. Inspect the folder contents and remove unsuitable captures before using it. Save/apply the configuration and restart the relevant vision task after changing templates. Reset the system if it is still using a previously loaded template set. Check the resulting object index whenever templates supply the type. Template indices follow the loaded filename order, starting at 0 ; they are not automatically matched to AI class names. Keep a clear mapping from each index to its pick filter and place destination, and recheck it after adding or renaming templates. An empty template folder cannot validate candidates. Confirm the saved cropped images are present before testing this workflow. Example cropped template: keep the full outline and minimize surrounding background. Build the vision pipeline ¶ Pass each result to the next block. See the Blockly program example for the block connections and test procedure. Follow these block connections and choose filter values for your objects. The values in the pictured draft are examples. Order Block Purpose 1 Get Detecting Image Read the calibrated detection image. 2 Filter HSV Keep pixels within the object’s color range. 3 Denoise Image Use morphology close/open as needed to fill small gaps and remove noise. 4 Find Contours Keep contours whose bounding-rectangle dimensions fall within the configured limits. 5 Find Rotation Objects From Contours Obtain candidate centers, sizes, and angles. 6 Match With Template Match candidates using the selected template folder. 7 Draw Rotated Objects To Image Draw the matched objects on the original detection image. 8 Convert To Tracking Object Convert the matched objects for the tracking system. 9 Push To Tracking Manager Make accepted objects available to the picking task. 10 Set Preview Image Display the annotated image for inspection. For white objects, the reference example uses lower HSV [0,0,160] and upper HSV [179,40,255] . Adjust these values to your lighting and material. The Find Contours fields are labeled Min area and Max area, but the current implementation compares both dimensions of the contour’s rotated bounding rectangle against these limits, in pixels. Set them for the object size at the current camera scale. Configure Match With Template ¶ Select the template folder, threshold, and match scale in the block. Connect its returned object list to both Draw Rotated Objects To Image and Convert To Tracking Object. Send this final list to tracking rather than the original color candidates. The block’s match scale is a percentage: 25% corresponds to 0.25 in System settings. The block returns the matched type, center, size, and angle, so verify template indices before assigning destinations. The System Template Matching switch stays off; this block performs the refinement. Check the program, save it, and run the vision-only task for the intended robot from Saved Tasks. docs.text: Capture templates with the same camera, detection crop, lighting, and object height used during operation. In DeltaXStudio, open Vision and select Template Matching mode. Create or select a template folder. In Images , select Cropped , open the live camera, place a representative object, and click Save Current Image . Capture a representative object into your template folder using Cropped camera images. Open Crop and select the saved image. Draw a tight rectangle containing the complete object, with minimal surrounding background. Click Crop & Save . This replaces that saved image with the cropped template. Use separate captures if you also need to keep the full frames. Repeat for the required reference objects. Inspect the folder contents and remove unsuitable captures before using it. Save/apply the configuration and restart the relevant vision task after changing templates. Reset the system if it is still using a previously loaded template set. Check the resulting object index whenever templates supply the type. Template indices follow the loaded filename order, starting at 0 ; they are not automatically matched to AI class names. Keep a clear mapping from each index to its pick filter and place destination, and recheck it after adding or renaming templates. An empty template folder cannot validate candidates. Confirm the saved cropped images are present before testing this workflow. Example cropped template: keep the full outline and minimize surrounding background.
